group_metadata.title: Empires of Ancient India: Dynastic Atlases, Battles & Inscriptions
group_metadata.subtitle: Geospatial Evolution of Sovereignty from the 16 Mahajanapadas to the Classical Golden Ages (600 BCE – 850 CE)
group_metadata.description: Interactive geospatial atlases mapping shifting imperial frontiers, decisive battlefields, and epigraphic records in Ashokan Brahmi, Classical Sanskrit, Ancient Greek, and Sangam Tamil. Verified from Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Memoirs, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum (CII), and peer-reviewed historical corpora.

battles.name: Magadha–Vajji War
battles.parties: Ajatashatru of Magadha vs. Licchavi / Vajji Confederacy
battles.summary: Ajatashatru deployed two groundbreaking military innovations: the Mahashilakantaka (heavy stone siege catapult) and the Rathamusala (chariot with revolving scythe blades). Ended the independence of Vaishali.
battles.source: Buddhist Digha Nikaya & Jaina Bhagavati Sutra

battles.name: Magadha–Kosala War of Kasi
battles.parties: Prasenajit of Kosala vs. Ajatashatru of Magadha
battles.summary: Protracted war over the revenues of Kasi; Prasenajit captured Ajatashatru but released him and concluded a matrimonial treaty, ceding Kasi permanently to Magadha.

battles.name: Annexation of Anga
battles.parties: Bimbisara of Magadha vs. Brahmadatta of Anga
battles.summary: Bimbisara stormed the port-capital of Champa, slaying King Brahmadatta and installing crown prince Ajatashatru as viceroy, opening Magadhan commerce to the sea.

battles.name: Avanti–Vatsa Border Wars
battles.parties: Chanda Pradyota of Avanti vs. Udayana of Vatsa
battles.summary: Pradyota ambushed King Udayana using a mechanical decoy blue elephant; resolved through the romantic marriage of Udayana and Vasavadatta.

battles.name: Siege of Viratanagara
battles.parties: Kuru-Trigarta Confederation vs. Matsya Kingdom
battles.summary: Susharma of Trigarta and the Kuru forces raided Matsya territory to capture cattle herds, repelled by Matsya cavalry and allied warriors.

battles.name: Dispute of the Rohini River
battles.parties: Shakya Republic vs. Koliya Republic
battles.summary: Severe drought triggered armed mobilization along the Rohini irrigation bund; averted without bloodshed through the personal arbitration of Gautama Buddha.

events.title: Crystallisation of the 16 Mahajanapadas across Northern & Central India
events.desc: Transition from Later Vedic tribal janas into sixteen sovereign territorial kingdoms (rajyas) and corporate republics (gana-sanghas) striking punch-marked silver karshapanas.

shloka.text: अङ्गा मगधा कासी कोसला वज्जी मल्ला चेती वंसा कुरु पञ्चाला मच्छा सुरसेना अस्सका अवन्ती गन्धारा कम्बोजा ति सोळस महाजनपदा ॥
shloka.transliteration: Aṅgā Magadhā Kāsī Kosalā Vajjī Mallā Cetī Vaṁsā Kuru Pañcālā Macchā Surasenā Assakā Avantī Gandhārā Kambojā ti soḷasa mahājanapadā ||
shloka.translation: Anga, Magadha, Kasi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Cedi, Vamsa, Kuru, Pancala, Matsya, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara, and Kamboja—these are the sixteen great realms.

events.title: Vaishali's Licchavi Republic Adopts 7,707-Member Assembly Governance
events.desc: The Vajji Confederacy institutes deliberative Santhagara assembly rule at Vaishali under elected executive magistrates, praised in Buddhist Nikayas.

shloka.text: जनपदतदवध्योश्च ॥ क्षत्रियात्समानशब्दाज्जनपदे तस्य राजन्यपत्यवत् ॥ सङ्घे चानौत्तराधर्ये ॥
shloka.transliteration: janapada-tad-avadhyośca || kṣatriyāt-samāna-śabdāj-janapade tasya rājany-apatyavat || saṅghe cān-auttarādharye ||
shloka.translation: A janapada state is named after its founding lineage; a republican Sangha operates corporately without superior-inferior royal autocracy.

events.title: Birth of Gautama Buddha in the Shakya Republic at Lumbini
events.desc: Siddhartha Gautama is born at Lumbini within the autonomous Shakya Gana-sangha bordering Kosala, later commemorated on Ashoka's stone pillar.

shloka.text: देवानंपियेन पियदसिना लाजिना वीसति-वसाभिसितेन अतन आगाच महीयिते हिद बुधे जाते सक्य-मुनी ति ॥
shloka.transliteration: Devānaṁpiyena Piyadasinā lājinā vīsati-vasābhisitena atana āgāca mahīyite hida Budhe jāte Sakya-munī ti ||
shloka.translation: Twenty years after his consecration, King Priyadarsin (Ashoka) came in person and worshipped here, declaring: 'Here Buddha the Sage of the Shakyas was born.'

events.title: Bimbisara Ascends Magadha & Builds Cyclopean Walls of Rajagriha
events.desc: Bimbisara founds the Haryanka dynasty, constructs 40 km dry-stone cyclopean fortifications around Girivraja, and builds Magadha's highway system.

shloka.text: स्वाम्यमात्यजनपददुर्गकोशदण्डमित्राणि प्रकृतयः ॥
shloka.transliteration: svāmy-amātya-janapada-durga-kośa-daṇḍa-mitrāṇi prakṛtayaḥ ||
shloka.translation: The sovereign ruler, ministers of state, populated territory, fortified citadel, public treasury, standing army, and allies are the seven constituent limbs of an empire.

events.title: Vardhamana Mahavira Propagates Jainism across Magadha, Anga & Videha
events.desc: The 24th Tirthankara organizes the four-fold Shramana order from Kundagrama and Rajagriha, anchoring Ahimsa and Anekantavada philosophy.

shloka.text: सव्वे पाणा पियाउया सुहसाया दुक्खपडिकूला । धम्मो मंगलमुक्किट्ठं अहिंसा संजमो तवो ॥
shloka.transliteration: Savve pāṇā piyāuyā suhasāyā dukkhapaḍikūlā | Dhammo maṅgalam-ukkiṭṭhaṁ ahiṁsā saṁjamo tavo ||
shloka.translation: All living beings cherish life, desire happiness, and recoil from pain. Non-violence, self-restraint, and austerity constitute the highest auspicious Dharma.

events.title: Magadhan Conquest of Champa (Anga) Opens Bay of Bengal Trade
events.desc: Bimbisara defeats Brahmadatta of Anga, securing the riverine emporium of Champa and eastern iron and copper mines for Magadha.

shloka.text: नानाश्रान्ताय श्रीरस्तीति रोहित शुश्रुम । पापो नृषद्वरो जन इन्द्र इच्चरतः सखा । चरैवेति चरैवेति ॥
shloka.transliteration: nānāśrāntāya śrīrastīti rohita śuśruma | pāpo nṛṣadvaro jana indra iccarataḥ sakhā | caraiveti caraiveti ||
shloka.translation: Fortune never favors one who refuses to strive forward; Indra himself befriends the tireless explorer—therefore march onward, march onward!

events.title: Dharmachakrapravartana at Sarnath & Dispatch of the First Sangha
events.desc: Gautama Buddha preaches the Four Noble Truths near Varanasi and sends sixty Arhat disciples outward along the Uttarapatha.

shloka.text: चरथ, भिक्खवे, चारिकं बहुजनहिताय बहुजनसुखाय लोकानुकम्पाय अत्थाय हिताय सुखाय देवमनुस्सानं ॥
shloka.transliteration: Caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṁ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ ||
shloka.translation: Walk forth, O monks, upon the wandering mission for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world.

events.title: Gandhara & Taxila Bridge Achaemenid Persepolis with Uttarapatha
events.desc: Taxila flourishes under scholars like Panini and royal physician Jivaka as the premier educational nexus connecting India with Western Asia.

shloka.text: एतद्देशप्रसूतस्य सकाशादग्रजन्मनः । स्वं स्वं चरित्रं शिक्षेरन् पृथिव्यां सर्वमानवाः ॥
shloka.transliteration: etaddeśaprasūtasya sakāśādagrajanmanaḥ | svaṁ svaṁ caritraṁ śikṣeran pṛthivyāṁ sarvamānavāḥ ||
shloka.translation: From the learned sages and academies nourished in this sacred heartland, peoples across the earth come to study character, ethics, and disciplined scholarship.

events.title: Ajatashatru Fortifies Pataligrama & Launches the Vajjian War
events.desc: Ajatashatru constructs a strategic fort at the Ganga–Son confluence and deploys Mahashilakantaka stone-catapults and scythed chariots.

shloka.text: तेन खो पन समयेन सुनिधवस्सकारा मगधमहामत्ता पाटलिगामे नगरं मापेन्ति वज्जीनं पटिबाहाय ॥
shloka.transliteration: Tena kho pana samayena Sunidha-Vassakārā Magadhamahāmattā Pāṭaligāme nagaraṁ māpenti Vajjīnaṁ paṭibāhāya ||
shloka.translation: At that very time Sunidha and Vassakara, the chief ministers of Magadha, built the fortified city at Pataligama to hold back the Vajjian confederacy.

events.title: Mahaparinirvana at Kusinara & First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha
events.desc: Under Ajatashatru's patronage, 500 elders recite the Sutta and Vinaya Pitakas inside Sattapanni Cave in Rajagriha.

shloka.text: हन्द दानि, भिक्खवे, आमन्तयामि वो—वयधम्मा सङ्खारा, अप्पमादेन सम्पादेथाति ॥
shloka.transliteration: Handa dāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo—vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādethāti ||
shloka.translation: Now indeed, O monks, I exhort you: all conditioned things are subject to decay; strive onward with tireless diligence.

events.title: Fall of Vaishali & Magadhan Unification of the Eastern Basin
events.desc: After a sixteen-year campaign, Magadha absorbs the Vajji Confederacy, shifting India's political gravity permanently from republics to centralized empire.

shloka.text: सं गच्छध्वं सं वदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानताम् ।
shloka.transliteration: saṁ gacchadhvaṁ saṁ vadadhvaṁ saṁ vo manāṁsi jānatām |
shloka.translation: Move together in harmony, speak with one voice, and let your minds apprehend alike in concord.

shloka_epigraph.text: अङ्गा मगधा च कासी च कोसलो वज्जी मल्ला चेती वंसा कुरु पञ्चाला मच्छ सुरसेना अस्सको अवन्ती गन्धारा कम्बोचा ति सोळस महाजनपदा।
shloka_epigraph.translation: These are the sixteen great realms: Anga, Magadha, Kasi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Ceti, Vamsa, Kuru, Pancala, Maccha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara, and Kamboja.

empires.historical_map_title: The Sixteen Mahājanapadas — India's First Republics & Kingdoms (c. 600–345 BCE)

detailed_history.overview: The emergence of the Sixteen Great Realms (Solasa Mahajanapadas) marked the Second Urbanisation of the Indian subcontinent (c. 600–345 BCE). Following the Later Vedic eastward migration along the Gangetic plain, iron smelting, wet-paddy rice cultivation, and coinage facilitated the transition from tribal chieftainships (janas) to sovereign territorial states (janapadas) and autonomous oligarchic republics (ganasanghas).

chronicle.era: c. 600 – 500 BCE: Rise of Territorial Monarchies & Ganasanghas
chronicle.narrative: The central and eastern Gangetic plain witnessed the crystallisation of sixteen paramount states, enumerated in Buddhist and Jaina canonical texts. Key monarchical kingdoms included Magadha (ruling from Girivraja/Rajagriha), Kosala (under King Pasenadi), Vatsa (ruled by Udayana at Kaushambi), and Avanti (under Pradyota at Ujjayini). Simultaneously, republican clans such as the Vajjian Confederacy (Licchavis of Vaishali), the Mallas of Kusinara, and the Shakyas of Kapilavastu governed through representative general assemblies (Santhagara).

chronicle.era: c. 500 – 400 BCE: Strategic Hegemony & Urban Guild Commerce
chronicle.narrative: The proliferation of punch-marked silver coins (Karshapanas / Puranas) and merchant guilds (shrenis) fueled overland trade along the Uttarapatha (Northern Highway connecting Taxila, Mathura, Kaushambi, Varanasi, and Pataliputra) and Dakshinapatha (Southern Highway to Pratishthana). The philosophical crossroads witnessed Gautama Buddha preaching across Magadha and Kosala, and Vardhamana Mahavira organizing Jain monastic order.

chronicle.era: c. 400 – 345 BCE: Magadhan Consolidation & Republican Absorption
chronicle.narrative: Through diplomacy and iron-age siege weapons (such as the Mahashilakantaka catapult and Rathamusala scythed chariot introduced by King Ajatashatru), Magadha systematically annexed Anga, Kosala, and the Vajjian confederacy, setting the stage for imperial consolidation under the Shishunagas and Nandas.

primary_sources.source_title: Aṅguttara Nikāya (Tika Nipāta / Mahāvagga, Sutta Piṭaka)
primary_sources.original_text: सोलस महाजनपदा: अङ्गा मगधा चेव कासी कोसलो तथा । वज्जी मल्ला चेती वंसा कुरु पञ्चाला मच्छा सूरसेना च अस्सका अवन्ती चेव गन्धारा कम्बोचा च ॥
primary_sources.transliteration: Solasa mahājanapadā: aṅgā magadhā ceva kāsī kosalo tathā | vajjī mallā cetī vaṁsā kuru pañcālā macchā sūrasenā ca assakā avantī ceva gandhārā kambojā ca ||
primary_sources.translation: These are the sixteen great realms: Anga, Magadha, Kasi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Cedi, Vamsa, Kuru, Pancala, Maccha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara, and Kamboja.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Pali Text Society (ed. Richard Morris), Anguttara Nikaya, Vol. I, p. 213; H.C. Raychaudhuri, Political History of Ancient India, Oxford University Press, 1996, pp. 85–130.
primary_sources.significance: Establishes the definitive canonical political geography of the subcontinent on the eve of the rise of Buddhism and the Magadhan empire.

primary_sources.source_title: Pāṇini, Aṣṭādhyāyī (Sutra 4.1.168 – 4.1.178)
primary_sources.original_text: जनपदतदवध्योश्च ॥ क्षत्रियात्समानशब्दाज्जनपदे तस्य राजन्यपत्यवत् ॥ सङ्घे चानौत्तराधर्ये ॥
primary_sources.transliteration: Janapada-tad-avadhyośca || Kṣatriyāt-samāna-śabdāj-janapade tasya rājany-apatyavat || Saṅghe cān-auttarādharye ||
primary_sources.translation: A political state (janapada) takes its appellation from the ruling warrior clan (Kshatriya); in a republican corporation (Sangha), governance operates without hierarchical monarchy (an-auttarādharya).
primary_sources.academic_citation: V.S. Agrawala, India as Known to Panini: A Study of the Cultural Data in the Ashtadhyayi, University of Lucknow, 1953, pp. 424–438.
primary_sources.significance: Contemporary grammatical and sociological proof of democratic/republican corporate governance (Sangha/Gana) operating alongside monarchical kingdoms.

capitals.role: Original mountain-ringed fortress capital of Bimbisara

capitals.role: Kalashoka's secondary imperial capital and Buddhist council venue
capitals.desc: Former Licchavi metropolis serving as northern administrative headquarters under the Shishunagas.

boundary_phases.phase: Mahapadma Nanda's Pan-North Indian Zenith (c. 340 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: First pan-North Indian empire stretching from Punjab (Beas River) across Kalinga to Bengal with a 200,000-strong standing army.

battles.name: Siege of Vaishali
battles.parties: Ajatashatru of Magadha vs. Licchavi Confederacy
battles.summary: 16-year siege concluded when Magadhan engineers deployed stone-hurling catapults (Mahashilakantaka) and scythed chariots (Rathamusala), permanently extinguishing Licchavi independence.

battles.name: Conquest of Avanti
battles.parties: Shishunaga of Magadha vs. Avanti Pradyotas
battles.summary: Shishunaga smashed the military power of Avanti, capturing Ujjayini and bringing western India under Magadhan suzerainty.

battles.name: Nanda Conquest of Kalinga
battles.parties: Mahapadma Nanda vs. Kings of Kalinga
battles.summary: Mahapadma Nanda invaded Kalinga, carried away the venerated Jina idol (Kalinga Jina) as an imperial trophy, and engineered the 300-year Tanasuliya canal.

battles.name: Mahapadma Nanda's Digvijaya
battles.parties: Mahapadma Nanda vs. Panchalas, Kashis, Kurus, and Ikshvakus
battles.summary: Systematic subjugation of old Aryan Kshatriya dynasties across northern India, earning Mahapadma the title Sarva-Kshatrantaka ('Destroyer of all Kshatriyas').

battles.name: Overthrow of the Shishunagas
battles.parties: Mahapadma Nanda vs. Kalashoka's Successors
battles.summary: Mahapadma seized power at Pataliputra, executing the ten sons of Kalashoka and inaugurating the Nanda dynasty's centralized imperial state.

battles.name: Deterrence at the Beas / Hyphasis
battles.parties: Nanda Imperial Army vs. Alexander's Macedonians
battles.summary: Intelligence of Dhana Nanda's 200,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, 2,000 chariots, and 4,000 trained war elephants provoked an army mutiny, forcing Alexander to abandon his march.
battles.source: Plutarch, Life of Alexander & Diodorus Siculus XVII.93

events.title: Bimbisara Founds Haryanka Dynasty in Magadha
events.desc: Consolidates marriage alliances with Kosala and Madra and institutes rural administrative headmen (Gramikas) across 80,000 villages.

shloka.text: दण्डः शास्ति प्रजाः सर्वा दण्ड एवाभिरक्षति । दण्डः सुप्तेषु जागर्ति दण्डं धर्मं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
shloka.transliteration: daṇḍaḥ śāsti prajāḥ sarvā daṇḍa evābhirakṣati | daṇḍaḥ supteṣu jāgarti daṇḍaṁ dharmaṁ vidurbudhāḥ ||
shloka.translation: Lawful governance rules all citizens and alone protects them; law stays awake while all sleep—hence the wise recognise rightful governance as Dharma itself.

events.title: King Udayin Establishes Pataliputra at the Ganga–Son Confluence
events.desc: Transfers the imperial capital from hill-ringed Rajagriha to river-fortress Pataliputra, commanding eastern fluvial commerce.

shloka.text: तेन खो पन समयेन सुनिधवस्सकारा मगधमहामत्ता पाटलिगामे नगरं मापेन्ति वज्जीनं पटिबाहाय ॥
shloka.transliteration: Tena kho pana samayena Sunidha-Vassakārā Magadhamahāmattā Pāṭaligāme nagaraṁ māpenti Vajjīnaṁ paṭibāhāya ||
shloka.translation: At that very time Sunidha and Vassakara, the chief ministers of Magadha, built the fortified city at Pataligama to hold back the Vajjian confederacy.

events.title: Shishunaga Ascends & Permanently Annexes the Avanti Empire
events.desc: Overthrows late Haryanka rule and defeats the Pradyota dynasty of Ujjayini, linking eastern India directly with western ocean trade routes.

shloka.text: ततश्च शिशुनाभः तत्पुत्रः काकवर्णो भविता... महानन्दिनस्ततः शूद्रागर्भोद्भवो महापद्मनामा नन्दः परशुराम इवापरोऽखिलक्षत्रान्तकारी भविष्यति ॥
shloka.transliteration: Tataśca Śiśunābhaḥ tatputraḥ Kākavarṇo bhavitā... Mahānandinastataḥ... Mahāpadmanāmā Nandaḥ Paraśurāma ivāparo'khila-kṣatrāntakārī bhaviṣyati ||
shloka.translation: After Shishunaga and Kakavarna, Mahapadma Nanda—wielding undisputed power like a second Parashurama—shall subjugate the warring Kshatriya houses and bring the realm under a single royal umbrella (Ekachhatra).

events.title: Second Buddhist Council Convened at Vaishali under Kalashoka
events.desc: Seven hundred elders convene to settle monastic Vinaya disputes at Valukarama under King Kalashoka (Kakavarna) Shishunaga.

shloka.text: सब्बपापस्स अकरणं कुसलस्स उपसम्पदा । सचित्तपरियोदपनं एतं बुद्धान सासनं ॥
shloka.transliteration: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā | Sacittapariyodapanaṁ, etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ ||
shloka.translation: To refrain from all evil, to cultivate what is wholesome, and to purify one's own mind—this is the teaching of the Awakened Ones.

events.title: Katyayana & Grammatical Standardization around Nanda-Era Academies
events.desc: Scholarly traditions refine Panini's Ashtadhyayi across Magadha and Kashi, codifying classical administrative Sanskrit.

shloka.text: विद्या ददाति विनयं विनयाद् याति पात्रताम् । पात्रत्वात् धनम् आप्नोति धनाद् धर्मं ततः सुखम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: vidyā dadāti vinayaṁ vinayād yāti pātratām | pātratvāt dhanam āpnoti dhanād dharmaṁ tataḥ sukham ||
shloka.translation: True learning bestows humility; humility confers capability; capability brings rightful prosperity; from prosperity springs Dharma, and from Dharma abiding felicity.

events.title: Mahapadma Nanda Founds Nanda Empire; Proclaims Himself 'Ekarat'
events.desc: Proclaims sole sovereignty ('Ekachhatra') and systematically annexes Ikshvaku, Panchala, Kashi, Haihaya, Kuru, and Surasena realms.

shloka.text: ततश्च शिशुनाभः तत्पुत्रः काकवर्णो भविता... महानन्दिनस्ततः शूद्रागर्भोद्भवो महापद्मनामा नन्दः परशुराम इवापरोऽखिलक्षत्रान्तकारी भविष्यति ॥
shloka.transliteration: Tataśca Śiśunābhaḥ tatputraḥ Kākavarṇo bhavitā... Mahānandinastataḥ... Mahāpadmanāmā Nandaḥ Paraśurāma ivāparo'khila-kṣatrāntakārī bhaviṣyati ||
shloka.translation: After Shishunaga and Kakavarna, Mahapadma Nanda—wielding undisputed power like a second Parashurama—shall subjugate the warring Kshatriya houses and bring the realm under a single royal umbrella (Ekachhatra).

events.title: Nanda Conquest & Canal Excavation in Kalinga (Hathigumpha Record)
events.desc: Mahapadma Nanda integrates Kalinga and constructs an extensive public irrigation canal commemorated three centuries later by King Kharavela.

shloka.text: पंचमे च दाणी वसे नंद-राज-ति-वस-सत-ओघातितां तनसुलिय-वाटा पनाडिं नगरं पवेसयति ॥
shloka.transliteration: Pañcame ca dāṇī vase Naṁda-rāja-ti-vasa-sata-oghātitāṁ Tanasuliya-vāṭā panāḍiṁ nagaraṁ pavesayati ||
shloka.translation: In his fifth regnal year, the king brought into the capital city by an aqueduct the water canal first excavated by King Nanda three centuries prior.

events.title: Standardization of Imperial Coinage & Nanda Fiscal Monopolies
events.desc: Dhana Nanda institutes uniform punch-marked silver karshapanas and systematic royal taxes across the Gangetic basin.

shloka.text: कौसलाधिप-पुत्रैश्च गङ्गा-गोदावरी-तटे । स्फुरद्-वीर्य-प्रतिष्ठाभिः धर्म-सेतुः प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
shloka.transliteration: (see Arthaśāstra 2.1.20) सह-उदकं आहार्यौदकं वा सेतुं बन्धयेत् । अन्येषां वा बध्नतां भूमि-मार्ग-वृक्ष-उपकरण-अनुग्रहं कुर्यात् ॥
shloka.translation: Let the state construct natural and canal-fed reservoirs (setu-bandha) across the realm, and aid civic builders with land, timber, and public protection.

events.title: Gangaridai–Nanda Standing Host Deters Alexander at the Beas River
events.desc: Reports of 200,000 infantry, 80,000 cavalry, 2,000 chariots, and 4,000–6,000 war elephants trigger the Macedonian mutiny at the Hyphasis.

shloka.text: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् । दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: śauryaṁ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṁ yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam | dānam īśvara-bhāvaś ca kṣātraṁ karma svabhāva-jam ||
shloka.translation: Valor, splendor, steadfast resolve, tactical skill, refusing flight in battle, generosity, and noble leadership are the innate duties of sovereign guardians.

events.title: Chandragupta Maurya & Chanakya Overthrow the Nanda Dynasty
events.desc: Revolt sparked against Nanda fiscality culminates in Chandragupta storming Pataliputra under Chanakya's strategic statecraft.

shloka.text: नवैतान्नन्दान् कौटिल्यो ब्राह्मणः समुद्धरिष्यति । तेषामभावे मौर्याः पृथिवीं भोक्ष्यन्ति । कौटिल्य एव चन्द्रगुप्तमुत्पन्नं राज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यति ॥
shloka.transliteration: nava-etān Nandān Kauṭilyo brāhmaṇaḥ samuddhariṣyati | teṣāmabhāve Mauryāḥ pṛthivīṁ bhokṣyanti | Kauṭilya eva Candraguptamutpannaṁ rājye'bhiṣekṣyati ||
shloka.translation: Chanakya (Kautilya) shall uproot the nine Nandas; thereafter the Mauryas shall govern the earth, and Kautilya himself shall consecrate Chandragupta Maurya upon the imperial throne.

shloka_epigraph.text: महापद्मपतिः कश्चित् नन्दः क्षत्रविनाशकृत् । ततो नृपा भविष्यन्ति शूद्रप्रायास्त्वधार्मिकाः ॥ एकराट् स महापद्मो ह्येकच्छत्रो भविष्यति ।
shloka_epigraph.translation: Mahapadma Nanda will arise, the destroyer of all Kshatriyas. He will be the sole sovereign (Ekarat) ruling under a single imperial parasol (Eka-chhatra).

sources.title: The Age of the Nandas and Mauryas
sources.author: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri

empires.historical_map_title: The Later Vedic Age — Janapadas of the Gangetic Plain (c. 1100–600 BCE)

detailed_history.overview: From the iron-rich forests of Rajagriha to the imperial citadel of Pataliputra, Magadha transformed from a regional kingdom into the dominant super-state of Northern India under the Haryanka, Shishunaga, and Nanda dynasties (c. 544–322 BCE). Mahapadma Nanda unified the Indo-Gangetic basin, establishing the first trans-regional empire governed by a standing army and centralized fiscal administration.

chronicle.era: c. 544 – 413 BCE: Haryanka Dynasty & Ajatashatru's Strategic Ascendancy
chronicle.narrative: Bimbisara forged dynastic alliances with Kosala and Madra and annexed the commercial port of Champa in Anga. His son Ajatashatru fortified Pataligram at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers and waged a 16-year campaign against the Licchavi republic, developing sophisticated military fortifications and the capital at Pataliputra.

chronicle.era: c. 413 – 345 BCE: Shishunagas & the Second Buddhist Council
chronicle.narrative: Shishunaga neutralized the centuries-old threat of Avanti, annexing Ujjayini to Magadha. Under his successor Kalashoka (Kakavarna), Pataliputra became the permanent imperial capital and hosted the Second Buddhist Council in Vaishali (c. 383 BCE).

chronicle.era: c. 345 – 322 BCE: The Nanda Empire & Imperial Monopolies
chronicle.narrative: Mahapadma Nanda overthrew the Shishunagas, crowned himself Ekarat (Sole Sovereign), and systematically conquered the Ikshvakus, Panchalas, Kashis, Haihayas, Kalingas, and Kurus. The Nandas amassed monumental wealth through taxation, state monopolies on salt and timber, and maintained a standing army of 200,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, and 4,000 war elephants—whose deterrent power forced Alexander the Great's troops to mutiny at the Beas river.

primary_sources.source_title: Diodorus Siculus, Bibliotheca Historica (Book XVII, Chapter 93)
primary_sources.date: c. 1st century BCE (citing contemporary Macedonian historians c. 326 BCE)
primary_sources.original_text: ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς τῶν Γανδαριδῶν τε καὶ Πρασίων ἔχει στρατιώτας πεζοὺς μὲν εἴκοσι μυριάδας, ἱππεῖς δὲ δισμυρίους, ἅρματα δὲ δισχίλια, ἐλέφαντας δὲ τετρακισχιλίους πολεμικῶς κεκοσμημένους.
primary_sources.transliteration: Ho de basileus tōn Gandaridōn te kai Prasiōn echei stratiōtas pezous men eikosi myriadas, hippeis de dismyrious, harmata de dischilia, elephantas de tetrakischilious polemikōs kekosmēmenous.
primary_sources.translation: The king of the Gangaridai and the Prasii (Magadha) was reported to have an army of 200,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, 2,000 four-horse chariots, and 4,000 elephants equipped and trained for war.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Diodorus Siculus, Library of History, Vol. VIII (Loeb Classical Library, Harvard University Press, 1963), pp. 384–387; R.C. Majumdar, The Classical Accounts of India, Firma KLM, 1981, p. 234.
primary_sources.significance: Contemporary western historical testimony confirming the unprecedented military scale of the Nanda imperial army that repelled Macedonian expansion east of Punjab.

primary_sources.source_title: Hāthīgumphā Inscription of King Khāravela (Line 6, Udayagiri Caves)
primary_sources.original_text: पंचमे च दाणी वसे नंद-राज-ति-वस-सत-ओघातितां तनसुलिय-वाटा पनाडिं नगरं पवेसयति...
primary_sources.transliteration: Pañcame ca dāṇī vase Naṁda-rāja-ti-vasa-sata-oghātitāṁ Tanasuliya-vāṭā panāḍiṁ nagaraṁ pavesayati...
primary_sources.translation: In the fifth year of his reign, His Majesty brought into the capital city by an aqueduct the canal opened by King Nanda (Nandaraja) three hundred years earlier...
primary_sources.academic_citation: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XX, pp. 71–89; D.C. Sircar, Select Inscriptions Bearing on Indian History and Civilization, Vol. I, University of Calcutta, 1965, pp. 213–221.
primary_sources.significance: Crucial inscriptional evidence documenting Nanda imperial hydraulic engineering and sovereign rule in Kalinga three centuries prior to Kharavela.

locations.desc: Former Licchavi metropolis serving as northern administrative headquarters under the Shishunagas.

locations.desc: Commanding maritime and overland routes linking North India to Arabian Sea ports.

locations.desc: Enclosed by monumental baked-brick ramparts with revetments and moats.

capitals.desc: Seat of imperial government where Alexander received embassies and died in June 323 BCE.

battles.name: Battle of the Granicus
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Persian Satraps & Greek Mercenaries
battles.summary: First major victory in Asia Minor. Alexander personally led the Companion Cavalry charge across the river, shattering Persian satrapal lines.

battles.name: Battle of Issus
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Darius III of Persia
battles.summary: Tactical masterpiece in a narrow coastal corridor along the Pinarus river; Darius fled leaving his royal family, chariot, and bow behind.

battles.name: Siege of Tyre
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Tyrian Fleet and Citadel
battles.summary: Seven-month siege in which Macedonians constructed a kilometer-long causeway from the mainland to storm the Phoenician island fortress.

battles.name: Battle of Gaugamela
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Darius III of Persia
battles.summary: Decisive battle of world antiquity. Alexander exploited a fatal gap in the Persian line with an oblique cavalry charge, destroying Achaemenid imperial power.

battles.name: Battle of the Persian Gate
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Satrap Ariobarzanes
battles.summary: Ariobarzanes held the narrow Zagros mountain pass in Persia's 'Thermopylae' until Alexander outflanked the defenders via mountain goat paths.

battles.name: Siege of the Sogdian Rock
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Oxyartes and Sogdian Barons
battles.summary: 300 elite Macedonian mountaineers climbed sheer icy precipices with iron tent-pegs at night, forcing Oxyartes' garrison to surrender without a fight.

battles.name: Siege of Aornos Rock
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Aspasioi and Assakenoi Warriors
battles.summary: Alexander conquered the legendary precipitous mountain stronghold above the Indus gorge that even Heracles was said to have failed to take.

battles.name: Battle of the Hydaspes
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. King Porus (Paurava Kingdom)
battles.summary: Epic night river crossing in a tropical monsoon storm. Alexander outmaneuvered Porus' 200 war elephants; Porus fought heroically until captured.
battles.source: Arrian V.8–19 & Plutarch, Life of Alexander 60

battles.name: Siege of Multan (Mallian Campaign)
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Mallian Republic (Malavas)
battles.summary: Frustrated by the siege pace, Alexander climbed the ramparts alone; his ladder broke and he was shot through the lung by a 3-cubit Indian arrow before rescue.

battles.name: Mutiny at the Hyphasis / Beas River
battles.parties: Macedonian Veterans vs. Alexander's Ambition
battles.summary: Exhausted after marching 20,000 km, Coenus and the army refused to cross the Beas to confront the 4,000 elephants of the Nanda Empire. Alexander built 12 altars and turned south.

events.title: Alexander Crosses the Hellespont & Triumphs at Granicus
events.desc: Alexander III of Macedon launches the Asian expedition from Macedonia across the Dardanelles against Achaemenid satrapies.

shloka.text: नानाश्रान्ताय श्रीरस्तीति रोहित शुश्रुम । पापो नृषद्वरो जन इन्द्र इच्चरतः सखा । चरैवेति चरैवेति ॥
shloka.transliteration: nānāśrāntāya śrīrastīti rohita śuśruma | pāpo nṛṣadvaro jana indra iccarataḥ sakhā | caraiveti caraiveti ||
shloka.translation: Fortune never favors one who refuses to strive forward; Indra himself befriends the tireless explorer—therefore march onward, march onward!

events.title: Victory at Issus, Siege of Tyre & Foundation of Alexandria in Egypt
events.desc: Breaks Darius III's royal line at Issus and establishes the maritime metropolis of Alexandria along the Nile delta.

shloka.text: उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः । न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः ॥
shloka.transliteration: udyamena hi sidhyanti kāryāṇi na manorathaiḥ | na hi suptasya siṁhasya praviśanti mukhe mṛgāḥ ||
shloka.translation: Tasks are accomplished solely through resolute exertion, never through passive wishes; prey never walks of its own accord into a sleeping lion's mouth.

events.title: Decisive Triumph at Gaugamela & Capture of Babylon
events.desc: Alexander's Companions break Achaemenid forces—including fifteen Indian war elephants sent by eastern satrapies—earning him 'King of Asia'.

shloka.text: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् । दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: śauryaṁ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṁ yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam | dānam īśvara-bhāvaś ca kṣātraṁ karma svabhāva-jam ||
shloka.translation: Valor, splendor, steadfast resolve, tactical skill, refusing flight in battle, generosity, and noble leadership are the innate duties of sovereign guardians.

events.title: Burning of Persepolis & Central Asian Campaign in Bactria–Sogdiana
events.desc: Crosses the Oxus into Maracanda (Samarkand) and captures the sheer fortress of the Sogdian Rock.

shloka.text: परिवर्तिनि संसारे मृतः को वा न जायते । स जातो येन जातेन याति वंशः समुन्नतिम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: parivartini saṁsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate | sa jāto yena jātena yāti vaṁśaḥ samunnatim ||
shloka.translation: In this revolving world, who is not born and does not perish? Truly born is he alone through whose deeds his dynasty and civilization ascend to enduring greatness.

events.title: Hindu Kush Crossing & Fierce Resistance by the Aspasioi and Assakenoi
events.desc: Alexander enters Swat and Bajaur (modern Khyber), encountering bitter hill-fortress defense at Massaga led by Queen Cleophis.

shloka.text: दण्डः शास्ति प्रजाः सर्वा दण्ड एवाभिरक्षति । दण्डः सुप्तेषु जागर्ति दण्डं धर्मं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
shloka.transliteration: daṇḍaḥ śāsti prajāḥ sarvā daṇḍa evābhirakṣati | daṇḍaḥ supteṣu jāgarti daṇḍaṁ dharmaṁ vidurbudhāḥ ||
shloka.translation: Lawful governance rules all citizens and alone protects them; law stays awake while all sleep—hence the wise recognise rightful governance as Dharma itself.

events.title: Storming of the Rock of Aornos & Pontoon Crossing at Ohind
events.desc: Crosses the Indus River via Hephaestion's pontoon bridge and receives diplomatic submission from King Ambhi at Taxila.

shloka.text: इमं मे गङ्गे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि स्तोमं सचता परुष्ण्या ।
shloka.transliteration: imaṁ me gaṅge yamune sarasvati śutudri stomaṁ sacatā paruṣṇyā |
shloka.translation: Accept my hymn of praise, O sacred rivers Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Sutudri (Sutlej), along with Parushni (Ravi), Asikni, and Vitasta (Jhelum).

events.title: Battle of the Hydaspes against King Porus of Paurava
events.desc: Monsoon clash along the swollen Jhelum; Porus's 200 war elephants stagger Macedonian cavalry before royal truce restores his crown.

shloka.text: स्वराष्ट्रे न्यायवृत्तः स्याद् भृशदण्डश्च शत्रुषु । सुहृत्स्वजिह्मः स्निग्धेषु ब्राह्मणेषु क्षमान्वितः ॥
shloka.transliteration: svarāṣṭre nyāyavṛttaḥ syād bhṛśadaṇḍaśca śatruṣu | suhṛtsvajihmaḥ snigdheṣu brāhmaṇeṣu kṣamānvitaḥ ||
shloka.translation: Within his own kingdom a ruler must uphold strict justice, be formidable against aggressors, unfailingly loyal toward allies, and compassionate toward scholars and citizens.

events.title: Army Mutiny at the Hyphasis (Beas) River Before the Nanda Host
events.desc: Exhausted troops halt east of Punjab upon learning of Magadha's vast war-elephant army; Alexander erects twelve monumental river altars.

shloka.text: प्र पर्वतानामुशती उपस्थादश्वे इव विषिते हासमाने । गावेव शुभ्रे मातरा रिहाणे विपाट् छुतुद्री पयसा जवेते ॥
shloka.transliteration: pra parvatānāmuśatī upasthād aśve iva viṣite hāsamāne | gāveva śubhre mātarā rihāṇe vipāṭ chutudrī payasā javete ||
shloka.translation: Forth from the mountain lap like eager mares freed from the tether, Vipas (Beas) and Shutudri (Sutlej) surge rapidly onward with gleaming waters.

events.title: Mallian Fortress Wound & Naval Descent Down the Indus
events.desc: Severely wounded storming Multan citadel; launches Nearchus's fleet from Pattala in the Indus Delta while marching across Gedrosia.

shloka.text: கடலோடா கால்வல் நெடுந்தேர் கடலோடும் நாவாயும் ஓடா நிலத்து ॥
shloka.transliteration: Kaṭalōṭā kālval neṭuntēr kaṭalōṭum nāvāyum ōṭā nilattu ||
shloka.translation: Even the stoutest-wheeled war chariot cannot sail across the ocean, nor can the sea-going merchant vessel run upon dry earth—master the proper arena of action.

events.title: Death of Alexander in Babylon & Birth of Greco-Buddhist Synthesis
events.desc: Sudden fever in Babylon fragments the empire among Diadochi, leaving Indo-Hellenistic garrisons that soon meet Chandragupta Maurya.

shloka.text: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वतोऽदब्धासो अपरीतास उद्भिदः ।
shloka.transliteration: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvato 'dabdhāso aparītāsa udbhidaḥ |
shloka.translation: Let noble thoughts and enlightening wisdom come to us from every quarter of the earth, unhindered and illuminating all.

shloka_epigraph.text:
«Ὦ παῖ, ζήτει σεαυτῷ βασιλείαν ἴσην· Μακεδονία γάρ σε οὐ χωρεῖ.»
«Ἀλέξανδρος ὁ Φιλίππου ὧδε κατέπαυσε τὸν δρόμον.»
shloka_epigraph.translation:
"O my son, seek a kingdom worthy of thyself; for Macedonia cannot contain thee." — Philip II to Alexander upon taming Bucephalus.
"Alexander son of Philip here called a halt to his course." — Inscription erected at the 12 Altars of the Hyphasis (Beas River).
shloka_epigraph.citation: Plutarch, Life of Alexander 6.5 & Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander V.29
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Loeb Classical Library, Harvard University Press

sources.title: Alexander the Great in the Punjab
sources.author: Buddha Prakash

empires.historical_map_title: After the Mauryas — Shungas, Greeks and Sakas (c. 185 BCE–50 CE)

detailed_history.overview: In 327–325 BCE, Alexander III of Macedon crossed the Hindu Kush into the northwestern Indus basin, initiating the first direct military confrontation between European Greco-Macedonian forces and the established kingdoms of ancient India. Encountering fierce resistance from the Aspasioi, Assakenoi, King Porus of Paurava at the Hydaspes, and the Mallian confederacy, the campaign ended when exhausted troops mutinied at the Hyphasis (Beas) river, initiating Greek settlement in Bactria and Punjab.

chronicle.era: 327 – 326 BCE: Siege of Aornos & Crossing the Indus
chronicle.narrative: Advancing through the Swat valley, Alexander assaulted fortified mountain citadels at Massaga and the legendary Rock of Aornos (Pir Sar). In early 326 BCE, the Macedonian army crossed the Indus at Ohind via a pontoon bridge constructed by Hephaestion, receiving submission and war elephants from King Ambhi (Taxiles) of Taxila.

chronicle.era: May 326 BCE: The Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum River)
chronicle.narrative: Facing King Porus on the opposite bank of the monsoon-swollen Hydaspes, Alexander executed a daring night river-crossing 27 km upstream. Despite the catastrophic impact of 200 Indian war elephants upon the Macedonian cavalry, Porus was outflanked and captured after fighting to the last. Impressed by Porus's royal poise ("Treat me as a king ought to treat a king"), Alexander restored his dominion and enlarged his territory.

chronicle.era: Autumn 326 – 325 BCE: Mutiny at the Hyphasis & Coastal Descent
chronicle.narrative: Upon reaching the Hyphasis (Beas River), Macedonian soldiers refused to advance further against the reported 200,000-man army of the Gangaridai and Nandas. Alexander erected twelve gigantic stone altars on the Beas bank to mark the eastern boundary of his empire, constructed a fleet on the Jhelum under Nearchus, and fought down the Indus through the Malli (Multan) before marching across the Makran desert.

primary_sources.source_title: Arrian of Nicomedia, Anabasis Alexandri (Book V, Chapter 18–19)
primary_sources.date: c. 140 CE (based on contemporary memoirs of Ptolemy I and Aristobulus, c. 320 BCE)
primary_sources.original_text: Ἀλέξανδρος δὲ προσελάσας πρῶτος ἤρετο αὐτὸν ὅ τι ἂν ἐθέλοι γενέσθαι οἱ· τὸν δὲ ἀποκρίνασθαι λόγος· "Βασιλικῶς μοι χρῆσαι, ὦ Ἀλέξανδρε."
primary_sources.transliteration: Alexandros de proselasas prōtos ēreto auton ho ti an etheloi genesthai hoi: ton de apokrinasthai logos: "Basilikōs moi chrēsai, ō Alexandre."
primary_sources.translation: Alexander rode up to him and asked how he wished to be treated. Porus replied: "Treat me like a king, Alexander." Alexander, pleased with his response, restored him to his sovereignty and added lands greater than his original kingdom.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander, Vol. II (Loeb Classical Library, Harvard University Press, 1983), pp. 62–67; A.B. Bosworth, Conquest and Empire: The Reign of Alexander the Great, Cambridge University Press, 1988, pp. 125–134.
primary_sources.significance: The definitive classical military chronicle recording the high chivalry and political sovereignty demonstrated during the Battle of the Hydaspes.

primary_sources.source_title: Plutarch, Parallel Lives: Life of Alexander (Chapter 62)
primary_sources.original_text: Ἡ δὲ πρὸς Πῶρον μάχη τῶν Μακεδόνων τὴν προθυμίαν ἤμβλυνε καὶ τῆς εἰς τοὔμπροσθεν πορείας ἐπέσχε... τοὺς δὲ Γανδαρίδας καὶ Πρασίους ἔφασαν προσμένειν μετὰ στρατιᾶς μυριάδων εἴκοσι πεζῶν.
primary_sources.transliteration: Hē de pros Pōron machē tōn Makedonōn tēn prothymian ēmblyne kai tēs eis toumprosthen poreias epesche... tous de Gandaridas kai Prasious ephasan prosmenein meta stratias myriadōn eikosi pezōn.
primary_sources.translation: The battle with Porus blunted the courage of the Macedonians and checked their further progress into India... for they learned that the kings of the Gangaridai and Prasii awaited them with 200,000 footmen, 80,000 horse, and 6,000 fighting elephants.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Plutarch, Lives: Demosthenes and Cicero, Alexander and Caesar (Loeb Classical Library, 1919), pp. 402–405; Robin Lane Fox, Alexander the Great, Penguin, 2004.
primary_sources.significance: Corroborates the psychological turning point where the Indian military reputation halted the Hellenic conquest at the river Beas.

locations.name: Pella (Macedonia)
locations.role: Macedonian royal birthplace of Alexander and expedition base
locations.desc: Argead dynastic capital where Aristotle tutored Alexander.

locations.name: Alexandria (Egypt)
locations.role: Mediterranean metropolis founded 331 BCE; tomb of Alexander
locations.desc: Imperial seaport and cultural capital designed by architect Dinocrates.

locations.name: Babylon (Mesopotamia)
locations.role: Administrative capital of Alexander's world empire
locations.desc: Seat of imperial government where Alexander received embassies and died in June 323 BCE.

locations.name: Taxila (Punjab)
locations.role: Indian headquarters and base for the Punjab expedition
locations.desc: King Ambhi surrendered his kingdom, providing 5,000 Indian troops and 30 war elephants.

locations.name: Persepolis (Persia)
locations.role: Achaemenid ceremonial capital; burned by Alexander
locations.desc: Grand palaces of Darius and Xerxes looted and burned in May 330 BCE.

locations.name: Susa (Elam)
locations.role: Persian administrative palace; site of the mass Susa Weddings
locations.desc: Alexander married Stateira and wed 80 Macedonian officers to noble Persian women.

locations.name: Bactra / Zariaspa
locations.role: Northern Silk Road fortress in Central Asia
locations.desc: Base for Sogdian campaigns; venue of Alexander's marriage to Roxana.

locations.name: Maracanda (Samarkand)
locations.role: Sogdian capital garrisoned by Macedonian troops
locations.desc: Site of the tragic drunken quarrel where Alexander killed Cleitus the Black.

locations.name: Alexandria the Furthest (Khujand)
locations.role: Northeastern frontier fortress on the Syr Darya (Jaxartes)
locations.desc: Built in 17 days to deter Scythian and Saka horse-archers.

locations.name: Alexandria in the Caucasus (Bagram)
locations.role: Hindu Kush operational base near Kabul
locations.desc: Founded 329 BCE at the foot of the Hindu Kush to control mountain passes.

locations.name: Alexandria Nicaea (Jhelum)
locations.role: Victory city founded after the Battle of the Hydaspes
locations.desc: Built on the eastern bank of the Jhelum to commemorate the defeat of Porus.

locations.name: Alexandria Bucephala
locations.role: City founded in memory of Alexander's war-horse Bucephalus
locations.desc: Erected on the western bank of the Jhelum where Bucephalus died of battle wounds.

locations.name: Alexandria on the Indus (Uch)
locations.role: Naval base at the convergence of the Punjab rivers with the Indus
locations.desc: Extensive dockyards built by Craterus and Hephaestion for 1,000 river vessels.

locations.name: Pattala (Indus Delta)
locations.role: Terminal ocean harbor on the Arabian Sea
locations.desc: Launchpad for Nearchus' fleet expedition sailing across the Indian Ocean to the Persian Gulf.

empires.name: Mauryan Empire & Pan-Indian Hegemony
empires.era_type: Largest Unified Empire in South Asian History
empires.religion: Buddhism (under Ashoka), Jainism (under Chandragupta) & Vedic Dharma

capitals.name: Pataliputra
capitals.role: Imperial seat of the Mauryas; city of 64 gates and 570 towers
capitals.desc: Monumental wooden and stone-pillared palatial capital described by Megasthenes.

capitals.name: Taxila (Uttarapatha)
capitals.role: Northern viceroyalty headquarters; Pan-Asian academy
capitals.desc: Governed by crown princes including Ashoka; nexus of Silk Road and Uttarapatha trade.

capitals.name: Ujjayini (Avantiratha)
capitals.role: Western viceroyalty headquarters on international highway
capitals.desc: Governed by Ashoka as viceroy; center of astronomical study and western trade.

capitals.name: Tosali (Kalinga)
capitals.role: Eastern viceroyalty following the Kalinga War
capitals.desc: Seat of the Kumara (royal prince) and site of Ashoka's Separate Rock Edicts at Dhauli.

capitals.name: Suvarnagiri (Dakshinapatha)
capitals.role: Southern viceroyalty in Karnataka
capitals.desc: Headquarters of the southern province managing royal gold mines (Hatti gold belt).

boundary_phases.description: Chandragupta Maurya unites Northern India, defeats Seleucus I Nicator, and expands frontiers to the Hindu Kush (Arachosia, Aria, Gedrosia).
Emperor Bindusara ('Amitrochates') consolidates imperial authority southward into the Krishna-Tungabhadra Deccan while maintaining cordial ties with Syria & Egypt.
Greatest extent of Mauryan power—including Kalinga, Gujarat, Afghanistan, and southern provinces down to Suvarnagiri, Maski, and Brahmagiri—governed by Dhamma.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Seleucid Empire (Antiochus II)
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Hellenistic successor empire of Seleucus I Nicator across Persia and Syria; concluded treaty with Chandragupta Maurya.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Greco-Bactrian Kingdom (Diodotus I)
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Greco-Bactrian kingdom founded by Diodotus I; hub of Hellenistic trade along the Oxus River.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Cholas, Pandyas, Cheras, Satiyaputras
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Sangam maritime dynasty on the Malabar coast; famous for pepper trade with Rome and Muziris port.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Tamraparni (Sri Lanka)
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Tamraparni (Sri Lanka): Contemporaneous frontier realm and trading partner.

battles.name: Overthrow of the Nanda Empire
battles.parties: Chandragupta Maurya & Chanakya vs. Dhana Nanda
battles.summary: Chandragupta assembled a mixed army of northwestern tribes, Greek mercenaries, and mountain allies to encircle and conquer Pataliputra, executing Dhana Nanda.

battles.name: Mauryan–Seleucid War
battles.parties: Chandragupta Maurya vs. Seleucus I Nicator
battles.summary: Seleucus crossed the Indus seeking to reclaim Alexander's conquests; Chandragupta repulsed the invasion. By treaty, Seleucus ceded Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae, and Aria in exchange for 500 war elephants.

battles.name: The Kalinga War
battles.parties: Emperor Ashoka vs. Republican Kalinga
battles.summary: Cataclysmic conflict along the Daya River. Over 100,000 Kalingans slain and 150,000 exiled. Witnessing the carnage prompted Ashoka's profound moral awakening and conversion to non-violence (Ahimsa).
battles.source: Ashoka Major Rock Edict XIII (Kalsi, Shahbazgarhi, Girnar)

battles.name: Bindusara's Deccan Campaign
battles.parties: Emperor Bindusara vs. Southern Peninsular Kingdoms
battles.summary: Bindusara (known to Greeks as Amitrochates, 'Slayer of Foes') marched across peninsular India, subjugating sixteen chiefdoms between the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal.

battles.name: Suppression of the Taxila Rebellion
battles.parties: Crown Prince Ashoka vs. Corrupt Provincial Governors
battles.summary: Citizens of Taxila rebelled against oppressive imperial ministers; Bindusara dispatched Prince Ashoka, who peacefully resolved the grievances without violence.

battles.name: Assassination of Brihadratha
battles.parties: Pushyamitra Shunga vs. Emperor Brihadratha
battles.summary: Mauryan Commander-in-Chief Pushyamitra Shunga killed the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha during an imperial military inspection, founding the Shunga Dynasty.

events.title: Chandragupta Maurya Founds Mauryan Empire with Chanakya's Counsel
events.desc: Liberates Punjab from Macedonian satraps and overthrows Nanda rule at Pataliputra, forging India's first subcontinental imperial administration.

shloka.text: नवैतान्नन्दान् कौटिल्यो ब्राह्मणः समुद्धरिष्यति । तेषामभावे मौर्याः पृथिवीं भोक्ष्यन्ति । कौटिल्य एव चन्द्रगुप्तमुत्पन्नं राज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यति ॥
shloka.transliteration: nava-etān Nandān Kauṭilyo brāhmaṇaḥ samuddhariṣyati | teṣāmabhāve Mauryāḥ pṛthivīṁ bhokṣyanti | Kauṭilya eva Candraguptamutpannaṁ rājye'bhiṣekṣyati ||
shloka.translation: Chanakya (Kautilya) shall uproot the nine Nandas; thereafter the Mauryas shall govern the earth, and Kautilya himself shall consecrate Chandragupta Maurya upon the imperial throne.

events.title: Codification of Kautilya's Arthashastra Saptanga Statecraft
events.desc: Establishes the seven-limbed theory of statecraft, intelligence bureaucracy, maritime tariffs, and agrarian irrigation under Rajadharma.

shloka.text: स्वाम्यमात्यजनपददुर्गकोशदण्डमित्राणि प्रकृतयः ॥
shloka.transliteration: svāmy-amātya-janapada-durga-kośa-daṇḍa-mitrāṇi prakṛtayaḥ ||
shloka.translation: The sovereign ruler, ministers of state, populated territory, fortified citadel, public treasury, standing army, and allies are the seven constituent limbs of an empire.

events.title: Mauryan–Seleucid Peace Treaty & Arrival of Ambassador Megasthenes
events.desc: Chandragupta defeats Seleucus I and receives eastern Iranian satrapies in exchange for 500 war elephants; Megasthenes authors the Indika.

shloka.text: देशः पृथिवी । तस्यां हिमवत्-समुद्र-अन्तरं उदीचीनं योजन-सहस्र-परिमाणं तिर्यक्चक्रवर्ति-क्षेत्रम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: deśaḥ pṛthivī | tasyāṁ himavat-samudra-antaraṁ udīcīnaṁ yojana-sahasra-parimāṇaṁ tiryak-cakravarti-kṣetram ||
shloka.translation: The land spanning northward from the Southern Ocean to the snowy Himalayas, measuring a thousand yojanas across, is the imperial Chakravartin domain.

events.title: Chandragupta Abdicates & Migrates to Shravanabelagola
events.desc: Entrusts the throne to Bindusara and journeys southward with Jain Acharya Bhadrabahu to Chandragiri hill in Karnataka.

shloka.text: सव्वे पाणा पियाउया सुहसाया दुक्खपडिकूला । धम्मो मंगलमुक्किट्ठं अहिंसा संजमो तवो ॥
shloka.transliteration: Savve pāṇā piyāuyā suhasāyā dukkhapaḍikūlā | Dhammo maṅgalam-ukkiṭṭhaṁ ahiṁsā saṁjamo tavo ||
shloka.translation: All living beings cherish life, desire happiness, and recoil from pain. Non-violence, self-restraint, and austerity constitute the highest auspicious Dharma.

events.title: Sudarshana Lake Reservoir Constructed in Saurashtra under Pushyagupta
events.desc: Mauryan provincial governor Pushyagupta constructs an engineered masonry dam at Girnar to regulate monsoon agriculture across Kathiawar.

shloka.text: कौसलाधिप-पुत्रैश्च गङ्गा-गोदावरी-तटे । स्फुरद्-वीर्य-प्रतिष्ठाभिः धर्म-सेतुः प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
shloka.transliteration: (see Arthaśāstra 2.1.20) सह-उदकं आहार्यौदकं वा सेतुं बन्धयेत् । अन्येषां वा बध्नतां भूमि-मार्ग-वृक्ष-उपकरण-अनुग्रहं कुर्यात् ॥
shloka.translation: Let the state construct natural and canal-fed reservoirs (setu-bandha) across the realm, and aid civic builders with land, timber, and public protection.

events.title: Bindusara Integrates Dakshinapatha up to Suvarnagiri & Maski
events.desc: Known in Greek courts as Amitrochates, Bindusara extends direct Mauryan provinces across the Deccan while trading peacefully with Cholas & Pandyas.

shloka.text: राज्ञो हि व्रतमुत्थानं यज्ञः कार्यानुशासनम् । दक्षिणा वृत्तिसाम्यं च दीक्षितस्याभिषेचनम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: rājño hi vratamutthānaṁ yajñaḥ kāryānuśāsanam | dakṣiṇā vṛttisāmyaṁ ca dīkṣitasyābhiṣecanam ||
shloka.translation: Energetic exertion is the sovereign's sacred vow; impartial administration is his ritual sacrifice; equality of treatment is his sacred offering; and his coronation is initiation into public duty.

events.title: Formal Consecration of Ashoka the Great at Pataliputra
events.desc: Ashoka is consecrated as Devanampiya Piyadasi; begins inscribing rock edicts dedicated to public welfare across India and Afghanistan.

shloka.text: नास्ति हि कम्मतरं सव्वलोकहितत्ता । य च किञ्चि पराक्रमामि अहं किंति भूतानां अनणं गच्छेयं ॥
shloka.transliteration: Nāsti hi kammataraṁ savvalokahitattā | Ya ca kiñci parākramāmi ahaṁ kiṁti bhūtānāṁ anaṇaṁ gaccheyaṁ ||
shloka.translation: There is indeed no higher duty than working for the welfare of all living beings. Whatever exertion I make is solely that I may discharge my debt to all creatures.
shloka.citation: Aśoka Major Rock Edict VI (Girnar, Gujarat)

events.title: The Kalinga War & Ashoka's Historic Turn to Dhammavijaya
events.desc: Following 100,000 battlefield deaths along the Daya River, Ashoka renounces aggressive warfare forever in Rock Edict XIII.

shloka.text: अठ-वसाभिसितस देवानंपियस पियदसिनो लाजिनो कलिग्या विजिता... ततो पछा अधुना लधेषु कलिगेषु तीवे धंम-वाये धंम-कामता च देवानंपियस ॥
shloka.transliteration: Aṭha-vasābhisitasa Devānaṁpiyasa Piyadasino lājino Kaligyā vijitā... Tato pachā adhunā ladheṣu Kaligeṣu tīve dhaṁma-vāye dhaṁma-kāmatā ca Devānaṁpiyasa ||
shloka.translation: Consecrated eight years, King Priyadarsin conquered Kalinga... After annexing Kalinga, the Beloved of the Gods conceived profound remorse and ardent devotion toward the practice and teaching of Dhamma.
shloka.citation: Aśoka Major Rock Edict XIII (Dhauli / Shāhbāzgaṛhī)

events.title: Kalinga Separate Edict I & Barabar Caves Dedication to Ajivikas
events.desc: Declares 'All human beings are my children' at Dhauli and carves mirror-polished granite caves in the Barabar Hills honoring all ascetics.

shloka.text: सब्बे मुनिस्सा पजा मम । अथा पजाय इच्छामि हकं किंति सवेण हित-सुखेन हिदलोकिक-पाललोकिकेन युजेवू ति ॥
shloka.transliteration: Sabbe munissā pajā mama | Athā pajāya icchāmi hakaṁ kiṁti saveṇa hita-sukhena hidalokika-pālalokikena yujevū ti ||
shloka.translation: All people are my children. Just as I desire for my own children that they be endowed with every welfare and happiness in this world and the next, so do I desire for all human beings.
shloka.citation: Aśoka Separate Kalinga Rock Edict I (Dhauli / Jaugaḍa)

events.title: Third Buddhist Council convened at Pataliputra under Moggaliputta Tissa
events.desc: Codifies the Abhidhamma Kathavatthu, safeguards Sangha unity on the Sarnath Pillar, and inspires the Lion Capital emblem.

shloka.text: देवानंपिये आनपयति... ये के भिक्खु वा भिक्खुनी वा संघं भाखति से ओदातानि दुसानि संनं धापयितु अनावाससि वासापेतविये ॥
shloka.transliteration: Devānaṁpiye ānapayati... ye ke bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā saṅghaṁ bhākhati se odātāni dusāni saṁnaṁ dhāpayitu anāvāsasi vāsāpetaviye ||
shloka.translation: His Majesty commands: the Sangha shall not be torn asunder by schism; whosoever divides the unified Order undermines the enduring harmony of the Dhamma.
shloka.citation: Aśoka Sarnath Lion Capital Schism Pillar Edict

events.title: Emissaries of Dhamma Dispatched across Eurasia & Sri Lanka
events.desc: Mahendra and Sanghamitra sail from Tamralipti to Sri Lanka while medical and ethical envoys reach Antiochus, Ptolemy II, and Antigonus.

shloka.text: देवानंपियो पियदसि राजा सवपासंडानि पूजयति पवजितानि च घरथानि च... सवपासंडानां तु साल-वढी अस ति ॥
shloka.transliteration: Devānaṁpiyo Piyadasi rājā savapāsaṇḍāni pūjayati pavajitāni ca gharathāni ca... savapāsaṇḍānāṁ tu sāla-vaḍhī asa ti ||
shloka.translation: King Priyadarsin honors all religious sects, both ascetics and householders, through gifts and reverence; for the growth of the essential core of every tradition is our true goal.

events.title: Assassination of Brihadratha & End of the Mauryan Dynasty
events.desc: After 137 years of Mauryan supremacy, Senapati Pushyamitra Shunga assumes power at Pataliputra following an imperial military review.

shloka.text: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । येनाक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत् सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: satyameva jayate nānṛtaṁ satyena panthā vitato devayānaḥ | yenākramantyṛṣayo hyāptakāmā yatra tat satyasya paramaṁ nidhānam ||
shloka.translation: Truth alone triumphs, never falsehood. Through truth is laid out the radiant path traversed by sages of fulfilled vows to the supreme treasure of reality.
shloka.citation: Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.1.6 (Inscribed beneath the Lion Capital of Ashoka)

shloka_epigraph.text: 𑀤𑁂𑀯𑀸𑀦𑀁𑀧𑀺𑀬𑁂𑀦 𑀧𑀺𑀬𑀤𑀲𑀺𑀦𑀸 𑀭𑀸𑀜𑀸 𑀯𑀻𑀲𑀢𑀺𑀯𑀲𑀸𑀪𑀺𑀲𑀺𑀢𑁂𑀦 𑀅𑀢𑀦 𑀆𑀕𑀸𑀘𑁆𑀘 𑀫𑀳𑀻𑀬𑀺𑀢𑁂 𑀳𑀺𑀤 𑀩𑀼𑀥𑁂 𑀚𑀸𑀢𑁂 𑀲𑀓𑁆𑀬𑀫𑀼𑀦𑀻𑀢𑀺 ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "King Devanampiya Piyadasi, when he had been consecrated twenty years, came here in person and worshipped, because here was born the Buddha, the Sage of the Shakyas. He caused a stone pillar to be erected and exempted the village of Lumbini from taxes."
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum (CII), Vol. I: Inscriptions of Asoka (E. Hultzsch, 1925, p. 164)

empires.historical_map_title: The First Empire — India under the Mauryas (c. 322–185 BCE)

detailed_history.overview: Founded by Chandragupta Maurya with the strategic counsel of Chanakya (Kautilya) in 322 BCE, the Mauryan Empire became the largest state ever established in the Indian subcontinent, spanning 5,000,000 km² from the Hindu Kush (Kandahar and Herat) to the borders of the Tamil realms. Under Ashoka the Great (r. 268–232 BCE), the empire embraced universal non-violence (Ahimsa), civic welfare, and the propagation of Dhamma across Asia and the Mediterranean.

chronicle.era: c. 322 – 297 BCE: Chandragupta Maurya & Seleucid Treaty
chronicle.narrative: Overthrowing the Nanda dynasty at Pataliputra, Chandragupta repelled the invasion of Seleucus I Nicator in 305 BCE. The resulting treaty ceded Arachosia (Kandahar), Gedrosia (Balochistan), and Paropamisadae (Kabul) to the Mauryas in exchange for 500 war elephants, sealed by a diplomatic marriage and the appointment of Megasthenes as Greek ambassador.

chronicle.era: c. 297 – 268 BCE: Bindusara & Trans-Peninsular Expansion
chronicle.narrative: Known to the Greeks as Amitrochates (Slayer of Foes), Bindusara extended imperial suzerainty southward into the Deccan plateau, maintaining diplomatic correspondences with Antiochus I Soter of Syria and Ptolemy II Philadelphus of Egypt.

chronicle.era: c. 268 – 232 BCE: Ashoka the Great & Imperial Dhamma
chronicle.narrative: In 261 BCE, Ashoka conquered Kalinga in a catastrophic war resulting in 100,000 casualties and 150,000 captives. Overcome by profound remorse, Ashoka renounced aggressive conquest (Digvijaya) in favor of moral conquest through righteousness (Dharmavijaya). He inscribed 33 Major and Minor Rock and Pillar Edicts across India, Pakistan, and Afghanistan in Prakrit (Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts), Greek, and Aramaic.

primary_sources.source_title: Ashoka Major Rock Edict XIII (Kālsī / Shāhbāzgaṛhī Version)
primary_sources.original_text: अठ-वसाभिसितस देवानंपियस पियदसिनो लाजिनो कलिग्या विजिता । दियढ-मित्रे पाण-सहसे ये ततो अपवुढे, सत-सहस-मित्रे तत हते, बहु-तावते वा मठे । ततो पछा अधुना लधेषु कलिगेषु तीवे धंम-वाये धंम-कामता धंमानुसथि चा देवानंपियस । सो अथि अनुसोचने देवानंपियस विजिति कलिग्यानि ॥
primary_sources.transliteration: Aṭha-vasābhisitasa Devānaṁpiyasa Piyadasino lājino Kaligyā vijitā | Diyaḍha-mitre pāṇa-sahase ye tato apavuḍhe, sata-sahasa-mitre tata hate, bahu-tāvate vā maṭhe | Tato pachā adhunā ladheṣu Kaligeṣu tīve dhaṁma-vāye dhaṁma-kāmatā dhaṁmānusathi cā Devānaṁpiyasa | So athi anusocane Devānaṁpiyasa vijiti Kaligyāni ||
primary_sources.translation: In the eighth year of his consecration, the Beloved of the Gods, King Priyadarsin, conquered Kalinga. One hundred and fifty thousand persons were carried away captive, one hundred thousand were slain, and many times that number perished. Thereafter, now that Kalinga is annexed, the Beloved of the Gods has turned eagerly toward the practice, love, and instruction of Dhamma. The Beloved of the Gods sorrows profoundly for the conquest of Kalinga.
primary_sources.academic_citation: E. Hultzsch, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. I: Inscriptions of Asoka, Archaeological Survey of India, 1925, pp. 66–70, 206–211; Romila Thapar, Asoka and the Decline of the Mauryas, Oxford University Press, 1997.
primary_sources.significance: The single most moving personal royal confession and unilateral imperial renunciation of war preserved from antiquity.

primary_sources.source_title: Megasthenes, Indika (Fragm. 34, preserved in Strabo XV.1.50–52)
primary_sources.original_text: Τῶν δ' ἀρχόντων οἱ μὲν ἀγορανόμοι εἰσίν, οἱ δ' ἀστυνόμοι, οἱ δ' ἐπὶ τῶν στρατιωτῶν... οἱ δ' ἀστυνόμοι εἰς ἓξ πεντάδας διαιροῦνται· οἱ μὲν τὰ δημιουργικὰ σκοποῦσιν, οἱ δὲ ξενοδοχοῦσιν, οἱ δὲ γενέσεις καὶ τελευτὰς ἀπογράφουσιν...
primary_sources.transliteration: Tōn d' archontōn hoi men agoranomoi eisin, hoi d' astynomoi, hoi d' epi tōn stratiōtōn... hoi d' astynomoi eis hex pentadas diairountai: hoi men ta dēmiourgika skopousin, hoi de xenodochousin, hoi de geneseis kai teleutas apographousin...
primary_sources.translation: Of the governing officials at Pataliputra, some oversee agriculture and forestry, others the army, and thirty commissioners oversee the municipality divided into six boards of five members each: the first inspects handicrafts, the second receives foreigners, the third registers births and deaths to ensure equitable tax collection, the fourth controls retail trade and measures, the fifth inspects manufactured goods, and the sixth collects the tithe on sales.
primary_sources.academic_citation: J.W. McCrindle, Ancient India as Described by Megasthenes and Arrian, Chuckervertty, Chatterjee & Co., 1926, pp. 86–91; Strabo, Geographica, Book XV (Loeb Classical Library, 1930).
primary_sources.significance: Eye-witness western documentary proof of the sophisticated urban bureaucracy and census accounting governing the Mauryan capital.

locations.name: Pataliputra
locations.role: Imperial seat of the Mauryas; city of 64 gates and 570 towers
locations.desc: Monumental wooden and stone-pillared palatial capital described by Megasthenes.

locations.name: Taxila (Uttarapatha)
locations.role: Northern viceroyalty headquarters; Pan-Asian academy
locations.desc: Governed by crown princes including Ashoka; nexus of Silk Road and Uttarapatha trade.

locations.name: Ujjayini (Avantiratha)
locations.role: Western viceroyalty headquarters on international highway
locations.desc: Governed by Ashoka as viceroy; center of astronomical study and western trade.

locations.name: Tosali (Dhauli / Kalinga)
locations.role: Eastern viceroyalty following the Kalinga War
locations.desc: Seat of the Kumara (royal prince) and site of Ashoka's Separate Rock Edicts at Dhauli.

locations.name: Suvarnagiri (Dakshinapatha)
locations.role: Southern viceroyalty in Karnataka
locations.desc: Headquarters of the southern province managing royal gold mines (Hatti gold belt).

locations.name: Alexandropolis / Kandahar
locations.role: Northwestern bilingual Ashokan rock edict site
locations.desc: Greek and Aramaic bilingual inscriptions by Ashoka commanding piety and vegetarianism.

locations.name: Girnar (Junagadh)
locations.role: Western provincial fortress and Sudarshana Lake dam
locations.desc: Engineered under Chandragupta by governor Pushyagupta and canalized under Ashoka by Tushaspha.

locations.name: Sannati
locations.role: Major Karnataka stupa complex with inscribed Ashokan portrait
locations.desc: Only known sculpted portrait inscribed 'Raya Asoko' discovered at Kanaganahalli.

locations.name: Sopara (Shurparaka)
locations.role: Chief Mauryan port on the Arabian Sea
locations.desc: Site of Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts VIII and IX engraved on basalt blocks.

locations.name: Tamralipti
locations.role: Eastern oceanic emporium on the Bay of Bengal
locations.desc: Port from which Princess Sanghamitta embarked carrying a sapling of the Bodhi tree to Sri Lanka.

locations.name: Sarnath (Isipatana)
locations.role: Site of the Lion Capital of Ashoka (National Emblem of India)
locations.desc: Erected by Ashoka to commemorate Buddha's First Sermon (Dharmachakrapravartana).

locations.name: Lumbini (Rummindei)
locations.role: Birthplace of Gautama Buddha
locations.desc: Ashoka's pillar inscription recording royal tax exemption ('lummini-game ubalike kate').

locations.name: Brahmagiri
locations.role: Southern Karnataka Minor Rock Edict site
locations.desc: Engraved by royal scribe Chapada in both Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts.

locations.name: Maski
locations.role: Edict confirming Ashoka's personal name
locations.desc: Famous Minor Rock Edict directly naming 'Devanampriya Asoka' discovered in 1915.

locations.name: Shravanabelagola
locations.role: Chandragupta Maurya's ascetic retirement sanctuary
locations.desc: Chandragiri hill where Emperor Chandragupta undertook the Jain rite of Sallekhana with Bhadrabahu.

empires.name: Post-Mauryan & Indo-Greek Kingdoms

capitals.name: Vidisha (Besnagar)
capitals.role: Primary Shunga imperial capital and cultural center
capitals.desc: Seat of Crown Prince Agnimitra; site of the Heliodorus Garuda pillar.

capitals.name: Pataliputra
capitals.role: Eastern Shunga imperial seat
capitals.desc: Retained as imperial capital by Pushyamitra Shunga following the Mauryan overthrow.

capitals.name: Sagala (Sialkot)
capitals.role: Indo-Greek capital of King Menander I (Milinda)
capitals.desc: Cosmopolitan Greco-Indian city celebrated for parks, moats, and Buddhist stupas in Milinda Panha.

capitals.name: Pushkalavati (Charsadda)
capitals.role: Western Indo-Greek mint and fortified administrative center
capitals.desc: Center of Hellenistic minting and Gandharan stone craft.

boundary_phases.phase: Menander I's Peak Indo-Greek Realm (c. 150 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Menander I (Milinda) ruled from the Paropamisadae and Arachosia across the Punjab to the Yamuna, striking refined bilingual silver drachms bearing Greek and Kharosthi inscriptions.

boundary_phases.phase: Shunga Empire in Central & Eastern India (c. 175 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Pushyamitra Shunga revived Vedic Ashvamedha sacrifices and patronized the reconstruction of the Sanchi Stupa gateways and Bharhut balustrades.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Satavahanas of Deccan
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Satavahanas of Deccan: Contemporaneous frontier realm and trading partner.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Kharavela of Kalinga
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Maritime eastern kingdom noted for elephant cavalry and oceanic trade with Southeast Asia.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Indo-Scythians (Sakas)
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Indo-Scythian rulers of Gujarat, Malwa, and Saurashtra; issued refined silver coinage.

battles.name: Battle of the Sindhu River
battles.parties: Prince Vasumitra (Shunga) vs. Indo-Greek Yavana Cavalry
battles.summary: Pushyamitra's grandson Vasumitra guarded the imperial sacrificial horse on the banks of the Sindhu, repelling Greek cavalry in a fierce engagement.

battles.name: Indo-Greek Siege of Saketa (Ayodhya)
battles.parties: Indo-Greek King (Demetrius / Menander) vs. Shunga Garrison
battles.summary: Yavana armies advanced deep into the Gangetic heartland, laying siege to Saketa and Mathura as recorded by the grammarian Patanjali.

battles.name: Greco-Bactrian March on Pataliputra
battles.parties: Menander I of Sagala vs. Shunga Imperial Forces
battles.summary: Menander's allied vanguard reached the mud-brick fortifications of Pataliputra before civil conflicts in Bactria forced the Greeks to retreat.

battles.name: Menander's Conquest of Mathura
battles.parties: Menander I vs. Surasena Chieftains
battles.summary: Indo-Greek annexation of the upper Yamuna valley, leaving hoards of Menander's silver drachms across the Mathura region.
battles.source: Archaeological Survey of India Coin Hoards

battles.name: Shunga–Vidarbha War
battles.parties: Crown Prince Agnimitra vs. King Yajnasena of Vidarbha
battles.summary: Agnimitra's general Virasena crossed the Narmada and defeated Yajnasena, partitioning Vidarbha between two cousin-rulers subject to Shunga suzerainty.

battles.name: Defense of Pushyamitra's Ashvamedha
battles.parties: Imperial Shunga Army vs. Regional Insurgents
battles.summary: Pushyamitra successfully concludes his second Ashvamedha sacrifice, reaffirming Vedic imperial rituals across northern India.

events.title: Pushyamitra Shunga Founds the Shunga Empire at Pataliputra & Vidisha
events.desc: Restores Vedic court rituals while presiding over monumental stone stupas and commercial prosperity along central India.

shloka.text: कोसलाधिपेन द्विरश्वमेधयाजिनः सेनापतेः पुष्यमित्रस्य षष्ठेन धनदेवेन धर्मराज्ञा पितुः फल्गुदेवस्य केतनं कारितम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: Kosalādhipena dvir-aśvamedhayājinaḥ senāpateḥ Puṣyamitrasya ṣaṣṭhena Dhanadevena dharmarājñā pituḥ Phalgudevasya ketanaṁ kāritam ||
shloka.translation: By Dhanadeva, righteous lord of Kosala, sixth in descent from General Pushyamitra who performed two Ashvamedha horse sacrifices, was this memorial monument erected.
shloka.citation: Ayodhyā Stone Inscription of King Dhanadeva

events.title: Demetrius I Crosses the Hindu Kush into Gandhara & Punjab
events.desc: Greco-Bactrian forces establish fortified twin-axis cities at Sirkap (Taxila) and Demetrias in Sind, minting bilingual Attic/Indian coinage.

shloka.text: यो सहस्सं सहस्सेन सङ्गामे मानुसे जिने । एकं च जेय्यमत्तानं स वे सङ्गामजुत्तमो ॥
shloka.transliteration: Yo sahassaṁ sahassena saṅgāme mānuse jine | Ekañca jeyyamattānaṁ sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo ||
shloka.translation: Though one conquer a million men upon the battlefield, he who masters his own spirit is the noblest victor of all.

events.title: Prince Vasumitra Guards Pushyamitra's Ashvamedha Horse on the Sindhu
events.desc: Immortalized in Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitram, young Vasumitra defeats Yavana cavalry patrols defending the imperial ritual steed.

shloka.text: इह अधीमहे, इह वसामः, इह पुष्यमित्रं याजयामः ॥
shloka.transliteration: iha adhīmahe, iha vasāmaḥ, iha Puṣyamitraṁ yājayāmaḥ ||
shloka.translation: Here we study, here we dwell, and here we officiate at the Ashvamedha sacrifice of Emperor Pushyamitra.

events.title: Consecration of the Stone Toranas & Medallions at Bharhut Stupa
events.desc: Master artisans of the Shunga realm transform timber stupa gates into narrative sandstone reliefs depicting Jatakas and royal processions.

shloka.text: प्रजासुखे सुखं राज्ञः प्रजानां च हिते हितम् । नात्मप्रियं हितं राज्ञः प्रजानां तु प्रियं हितम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: prajāsukhe sukhaṁ rājñaḥ prajānāṁ ca hite hitam | nātmapriyaṁ hitaṁ rājñaḥ prajānāṁ tu priyaṁ hitam ||
shloka.translation: In the happiness of the subjects lies the happiness of the sovereign; in their welfare rests his own welfare. Not what pleases himself, but what uplifts his people is the king's good.

events.title: King Menander I (Milinda) Unifies Punjab & Reaches Mathura
events.desc: From his bustling capital at Sagala (Sialkot), Menander mints brilliant silver drachms in Greek and Kharosthi styling himself 'Soter' and 'Dharmika'.

shloka.text: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वतोऽदब्धासो अपरीतास उद्भिदः ।
shloka.transliteration: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvato 'dabdhāso aparītāsa udbhidaḥ |
shloka.translation: Let noble thoughts and enlightening wisdom come to us from every quarter of the earth, unhindered and illuminating all.

events.title: Sage Patanjali Composes the Vyākaraṇa Mahābhāṣya
events.desc: Citing 'Here we sacrifice for Pushyamitra' as a contemporaneous grammatical example, Patanjali completes India's monumental Sanskrit linguistic commentary.

shloka.text: विद्या ददाति विनयं विनयाद् याति पात्रताम् । पात्रत्वात् धनम् आप्नोति धनाद् धर्मं ततः सुखम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: vidyā dadāti vinayaṁ vinayād yāti pātratām | pātratvāt dhanam āpnoti dhanād dharmaṁ tataḥ sukham ||
shloka.translation: True learning bestows humility; humility confers capability; capability brings rightful prosperity; from prosperity springs Dharma, and from Dharma abiding felicity.

events.title: Philosophical Dialogues of Milindapañha at Sagala
events.desc: King Menander debates Buddhist monk Nagasena across subtle questions of self, ethics, and statecraft, embracing the Dhamma.

shloka.text: न हि वेरेन वेरानि सम्मन्तीध कुदाचनं । अवेरेन च सम्मन्ति एस धम्मो सनन्तनो ॥
shloka.transliteration: Na hi verena verāni sammantīdha kudācanaṁ | Averena ca sammanti esa dhammo sanantano ||
shloka.translation: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world; by non-hatred alone is hatred pacified—this is the eternal law.

events.title: Expansion & Marble Railings of the Great Stupa at Sanchi
events.desc: Under Shunga patronage, civic guilds from Vidisha double the brick core of Sanchi Stupa I and encase it in dressed sandstone.

shloka.text: सब्बपापस्स अकरणं कुसलस्स उपसम्पदा । सचित्तपरियोदपनं एतं बुद्धान सासनं ॥
shloka.transliteration: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā | Sacittapariyodapanaṁ, etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ ||
shloka.translation: To refrain from all evil, to cultivate what is wholesome, and to purify one's own mind—this is the teaching of the Awakened Ones.

events.title: Heliodorus, Greek Envoy from Taxila, Erects Garuda Pillar at Vidisha
events.desc: Ambassador Heliodorus proclaims himself a 'Bhagavata' in Early Brahmi and inscribes ethical tenets drawn from the Mahabharata.

shloka.text: देवदेवस वासुदेवस गरुडध्वजे अयं कारिते इअ हेलियोदोरेण भागवतेन... त्रीणि अमृतपदानि सु-अनुष्ठितानि नयन्ति स्वर्गम्—दम त्याग अप्रमाद ॥
shloka.transliteration: Devadevasa Vāsudevasa garuḍadhvaje ayaṁ kārite ia Heliodoreṇa bhāgavatena... trīṇi amṛtapadāni su-anuṣṭhitāni nayanti svargam—dama tyāga apramāda ||
shloka.translation: This Garuda pillar of Vasudeva was erected by Heliodorus, Greek envoy from Taxila and devotee of Vishnu... Three immortal steps lead to heaven when practiced well: Self-restraint, Renunciation, and Vigilance.
shloka.citation: Heliodorus Pillar Inscription, Besnagar (Vidisha, c. 113 BCE)

events.title: Kanva Transition & Indo-Scythian Eclipse in the Northwest
events.desc: Minister Vasudeva Kanva succeeds the Shungas in Magadha, while Maues and Rajuvula establish Saka satrapies across Punjab and Mathura.

shloka.text: परिवर्तिनि संसारे मृतः को वा न जायते । स जातो येन जातेन याति वंशः समुन्नतिम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: parivartini saṁsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate | sa jāto yena jātena yāti vaṁśaḥ samunnatim ||
shloka.translation: In this revolving world, who is not born and does not perish? Truly born is he alone through whose deeds his dynasty and civilization ascend to enduring greatness.

shloka_epigraph.text: 𑀤𑁂𑀯𑀤𑁂𑀯𑀲 𑀯𑀸𑀲𑀼𑀤𑁂𑀯𑀲 𑀕𑀭𑀼𑀟𑀥𑁆𑀯𑀚𑁄 𑀅𑀬𑀁 𑀓𑀸𑀭𑀺𑀢𑁄 𑀇𑀬 𑀳𑁂𑀮𑀺𑀑𑀤𑁄𑀭𑁂𑀡 𑀪𑀸𑀕𑀯𑀢𑁂𑀦... 𑀢𑁆𑀭𑀻𑀦𑀺 𑀅𑀫𑀼𑀢𑀧𑀤𑀸𑀦𑀺 𑀲𑀼𑀅𑀦𑀼𑀞𑀺𑀢𑀸𑀦𑀺 𑀦𑀬𑀁𑀢𑀺 𑀲𑀕𑀁 — 𑀤𑀫𑁄 𑀘𑀸𑀕𑁄 𑀅𑀧𑁆𑀭𑀫𑀸𑀤𑁄 ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "This Garuda column of Vasudeva, the God of gods, was erected here by Heliodorus, a Bhagavata, son of Dion and inhabitant of Taxila, who came as Greek ambassador from King Antialcidas to King Bhagabhadra... Three are the immortal steps which lead to heaven when well observed: Self-restraint (Dama), Renunciation (Tyaga), and Vigilance (Apramada)."
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Archaeological Survey of India, Annual Report 1908–1909, pp. 126–129

empires.historical_map_title: After the Mauryas — Shungas, Greeks and Sakas (c. 185 BCE–50 CE)

detailed_history.overview: The post-Mauryan epoch (c. 185 BCE – 50 CE) witnessed dynamic cross-cultural integration across northwestern and central India. While Pushyamitra Shunga founded the Shunga Dynasty at Pataliputra and Vidisha, revitalizing Vedic sacrificial rites (Ashvamedha) and patronizing Buddhist art at Bharhut, the Indo-Greek kings (Yavanas) under Menander I (Milinda) ruled Punjab, Gandhara, and the Kabul valley, fusing Hellenistic realism with Buddhist philosophy.

chronicle.era: c. 185 – 150 BCE: Pushyamitra Shunga & Vedic Restoration
chronicle.narrative: Pushyamitra Shunga, commander-in-chief (Senapati) of the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha, took the throne in 185 BCE. He celebrated two Ashvamedha horse sacrifices at Ayodhya, repelled incursions along the Sindhu river, and patronized the construction of the monumental stone railings and toranas at Bharhut Stupa.

chronicle.era: c. 165 – 130 BCE: Menander I (Milinda) & Greco-Buddhism
chronicle.narrative: From his capital at Sagala (Sialkot), the Greco-Bactrian king Menander I expanded his realm across Punjab and the Gangetic borders. His philosophical dialogues with the Buddhist monk Nagasena, recorded in the canonical Pali text Milindapañha, culminated in Menander embracing Buddhism and minting bilingual coins featuring the Greek legend and Kharosthi Prakrit 'Dharmikasa' (Follower of the Dharma).

chronicle.era: c. 115 – 50 BCE: Heliodorus Pillar & Cultural Syncretism
chronicle.narrative: In c. 113 BCE, the Greek king Antialcidas of Taxila dispatched ambassador Heliodorus to the court of King Bhagabhadra Shunga at Vidisha (Besnagar). Heliodorus dedicated a monolithic Garuda pillar to Vasudeva-Krishna, describing himself as a Bhagavata in early Brahmi script.

primary_sources.source_title: Heliodorus Garuda Pillar Inscription (Besnagar, Vidisha)
primary_sources.original_text: देवदेवस वासुदेवस गरुडध्वजे अयं कारिते इअ हेलियोदोरेण भागवतेन दियस पुत्रेण तखसिलाकेन योन-दूतेन आगतेन... त्रीणि अमृत-पदानि सु-अनुष्ठितानि नयंति स्वर्गं: दम त्याग अप्रमाद ॥
primary_sources.transliteration: Devadevasa Vāsudevasa garuḍadhvaje ayaṁ kārite ia Heliodoreṇa bhāgavatena Diyasa putreṇa Takhasilākena Yona-dūtena āgatena... Trīṇi amuta-padāni su-anuṣṭhitāni nayaṁti svagaṁ: dama tyāga apramāda ||
primary_sources.translation: This Garuda column of Vasudeva, the God of gods, was erected here by Heliodorus, a Bhagavata (devotee of Vishnu), son of Dion, an inhabitant of Taxila, who came as Greek ambassador from King Antialcidas to King Kasiputra Bhagabhadra... Three are the immortal steps which when well practiced lead to heaven: Self-restraint (Dama), Renunciation (Tyaga), and Vigilance (Apramada).
primary_sources.academic_citation: Archaeological Survey of India Annual Report 1908–1909, pp. 126–129; D.C. Sircar, Select Inscriptions Bearing on Indian History and Civilization, Vol. I, 1965, pp. 88–90.
primary_sources.significance: The oldest surviving monumental epigraphic proof of a Greek citizen adopting Vaishnava Hinduism and citing ethical tenets from the Mahabharata.

primary_sources.source_title: Ayodhyā Inscription of King Dhanadeva
primary_sources.original_text: कोसलाधिपेन द्विरश्वमेध-याजिनः सेनापतेः पुष्यमित्रस्य षष्ठेन... धनदेवेन धर्मराज्ञा पितुः फल्गुदेवस्य केतनं कारितम् ॥
primary_sources.transliteration: Kosalādhipena dvir-aśvamedha-yājinaḥ senāpateḥ Puṣyamitrasya ṣaṣṭhena... Dhanadevena dharmarājñā pituḥ Phalgudevasya ketanaṁ kāritam ||
primary_sources.translation: By the ruler of Kosala, Dhanadeva, the righteous king, sixth in descent from the Commander-in-Chief Pushyamitra who celebrated two Ashvamedha horse sacrifices, this memorial was caused to be made for his father Phalgudeva.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XX, p. 57; K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, A Comprehensive History of India, Vol. II, Orient Longmans, 1957, pp. 95–98.
primary_sources.significance: Inscriptional confirmation of Pushyamitra Shunga's title Senapati and his celebration of two classical Vedic imperial sacrifices.
