events.title: King Simuka Founds the Satavahana Dynasty at Pratishthana
events.desc: Establishes independent Andhra–Satavahana rule in the Godavari valley, creating an economic bridge between North India and Tamilakam.

shloka.text: माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः ॥
shloka.transliteration: mātā bhūmiḥ putro ahaṁ pṛthivyāḥ ||
shloka.translation: The Earth is my nurturing Mother, and I am a devoted son of this sacred land.

events.title: Satakarni I & Queen Nayanika's Naneghat Pass Rock Inscription
events.desc: Commemorates two Ashvamedha and Rajasuya sacrifices, featuring the earliest stone portrait gallery and proto-Brahmi decimal numerals.

shloka.text: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् । दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: śauryaṁ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṁ yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam | dānam īśvara-bhāvaś ca kṣātraṁ karma svabhāva-jam ||
shloka.translation: Valor, splendor, steadfast resolve, tactical skill, refusing flight in battle, generosity, and noble leadership are the innate duties of sovereign guardians.

events.title: Subjugation of Magadhan Kanvas & Malwa Trade Integration
events.desc: Satavahana armies push northward across the Narmada toward Vidisha, securing overland caravan access along the Dakshinapatha.

shloka.text: स्वराष्ट्रे न्यायवृत्तः स्याद् भृशदण्डश्च शत्रुषु । सुहृत्स्वजिह्मः स्निग्धेषु ब्राह्मणेषु क्षमान्वितः ॥
shloka.transliteration: svarāṣṭre nyāyavṛttaḥ syād bhṛśadaṇḍaśca śatruṣu | suhṛtsvajihmaḥ snigdheṣu brāhmaṇeṣu kṣamānvitaḥ ||
shloka.translation: Within his own kingdom a ruler must uphold strict justice, be formidable against aggressors, unfailingly loyal toward allies, and compassionate toward scholars and citizens.

events.title: King Hala Compiles the Maharashtri Prakrit Anthology Gāthā Sattasaī
events.desc: Seven hundred lyrical verses celebrating pastoral life, seasons, and rural affection across the Deccan plateau.

shloka.text: परिवर्तिनि संसारे मृतः को वा न जायते । स जातो येन जातेन याति वंशः समुन्नतिम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: parivartini saṁsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate | sa jāto yena jātena yāti vaṁśaḥ samunnatim ||
shloka.translation: In this revolving world, who is not born and does not perish? Truly born is he alone through whose deeds his dynasty and civilization ascend to enduring greatness.

events.title: Monumental Excavation of the Great Chaitya at Karle & Kanheri Caves
events.desc: Merchants and guilds from Sopara and Kalyan carve the grandest Hinayana rock-cut Buddhist prayer halls in the Western Ghats.

shloka.text: सब्बपापस्स अकरणं कुसलस्स उपसम्पदा । सचित्तपरियोदपनं एतं बुद्धान सासनं ॥
shloka.transliteration: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā | Sacittapariyodapanaṁ, etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ ||
shloka.translation: To refrain from all evil, to cultivate what is wholesome, and to purify one's own mind—this is the teaching of the Awakened Ones.

events.title: Reign of Gautamiputra Satakarni & Battle of Govardhana (Nashik)
events.desc: Shatters the Kshaharata Saka power of Nahapana, counter-striking the 13,000-coin Jogalthambi silver hoard in victory.

shloka.text: सक-यवन-पल्हव-निसूदनस खखरात-वस-निरवसेस-करस सातवाहन-कुल-यस-पतिठापन-करस... तिसमुद-तोय-पीत-वाहनस ॥
shloka.transliteration: Saka-Yavana-Palhava-nisūdanasa Khakharāta-vasa-niravasesa-karasa Sātavāhana-kula-yasa-patiṭhāpana-karasa... tisamuda-toya-pīta-vāhanasa ||
shloka.translation: Destroyer of the Sakas, Yavanas, and Pahlavas; restorer of the Satavahana lineage; whose royal war-chargers drank from the waters of the three encircling oceans.
shloka.citation: Nāsik Cave 3 Inscription of Gautamī Balaśrī

events.title: Amaravati Great Stupa Enlarged under Vashishthiputra Pulumavi
events.desc: Shifts political weight toward Dharanikota on the Krishna river, adorning the Amaravati Mahachaitya in carved limestone reliefs.

shloka.text: धर्मो विश्वस्य जगतः प्रतिष्ठा लोके धर्मिष्ठं प्रजा उपसर्पन्ति । धर्मेण पापमपनुदन्ति धर्मे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: dharmo viśvasya jagataḥ pratiṣṭhā loke dharmiṣṭhaṁ prajā upasarpanti | dharmeṇa pāpam-apanudanti dharme sarvaṁ pratiṣṭhitam ||
shloka.translation: Dharma is the sustaining foundation of the entire cosmos; citizens gravitate toward the righteous guardian; all civilization stands anchored in Dharma.

events.title: Diplomatic Marriage & Shaka–Satavahana Treaties at Girnar
events.desc: Western Kshatrapa King Rudradaman I notes twice sparing Vashishthiputra Satakarni because of close marital kinship.

shloka.text: दक्षिणापथपतेः सातकर्णेर्द्विरपि निर्व्याजमवजीत्यावजीत्य संबन्धविदूरताया अनुत्सादनात्प्राप्तयशसा ॥
shloka.transliteration: Dakṣiṇāpathapateḥ Sātakarṇer-dvir-api nirvyājam-avajītyā-vajītya saṁbandha-vidūratāyā anutsādanāt-prāptayaśasā ||
shloka.translation: Having twice fairly defeated Satakarni, Lord of Dakshinapatha, yet refraining from his utter destruction owing to close dynastic marriage ties—while reconstructing the breached Sudarshana dam.
shloka.citation: Junāgaḍh Rock Inscription of Rudradāman I (150 CE)

events.title: Yajna Sri Satakarni Mints Two-Masted Ship Coins for Maritime Trade
events.desc: Issues iconic silver and lead currency depicting rigged ocean-going vessels sailing from Sopara, Bharuch, and Ghantasala.

shloka.text: கடலோடா கால்வல் நெடுந்தேர் கடலோடும் நாவாயும் ஓடா நிலத்து ॥
shloka.transliteration: Kaṭalōṭā kālval neṭuntēr kaṭalōṭum nāvāyum ōṭā nilattu ||
shloka.translation: Even the stoutest-wheeled war chariot cannot sail across the ocean, nor can the sea-going merchant vessel run upon dry earth—master the proper arena of action.

events.title: Acharya Nagarjuna & Rise of the Sriparvata University at Nagarjunakonda
events.desc: Master philosopher Nagarjuna expounds Madhyamaka Shunyata along the Krishna Valley, laying foundations for Ikshvaku & Chalukya successors.

shloka.text: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
shloka.transliteration: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṁ pavitramiha vidyate |
shloka.translation: In all this world there exists no purifier equal to luminous knowledge and scholarly inquiry.

shloka_epigraph.text: 𑀭𑀸𑀜𑁄 𑀕𑁄𑀢𑀫𑀻𑀧𑀼𑀢𑀲 𑀲𑀸𑀢𑀓𑀡𑀺𑀲... 𑀔𑀔𑀭𑀸𑀢𑀯𑀲𑀦𑀺𑀭𑁆𑀯𑀲𑁂𑀲𑀓𑀭𑀲 𑀲𑀸𑀢𑀯𑀸𑀳𑀦𑀓𑀼𑀮𑀬𑀲𑀧𑀢𑀺𑀞𑀸𑀧𑀦𑀓𑀭𑀲 𑀢𑁆𑀭𑀺𑀲𑀫𑀼𑀤𑁆𑀭𑀢𑁄𑀬𑀧𑀻𑀢𑀯𑀸𑀳𑀦𑀲 ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "Of King Gautamiputra Satakarni... who destroyed the pride and arrogance of the Kshatriyas, who completely eradicated the Kshaharata lineage, who restored the glory of the Satavahana dynasty, whose chargers drank the waters of the three oceans (Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, and Indian Ocean)."
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. VIII, pp. 60–65 (E. Senart, 1905)

empires.historical_map_title: The Deccan Bridge — the Sātavāhana Age (c. 100 BCE–220 CE)

detailed_history.overview: The Sātavāhana Dynasty (Andhras, c. 100 BCE – 225 CE) ruled the Deccan plateau spanning Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh from twin capitals at Pratishthana (Paithan) and Amaravati (Dhanyakataka). Guardians of the trans-peninsular trade routes linking the western ports (Kalyan, Sopara, Chaul) with the eastern Bay of Bengal, the Satavahanas were celebrated for their matronymic titles, cave temples at Karle, Kanheri, and Nasik, and the Great Stupa of Amaravati.

chronicle.era: c. 100 – 50 BCE: Simuka & Early Deccan Hegemony
chronicle.narrative: Simuka founded the dynasty in the Godavari basin following the decline of the Mauryas and Kanvas. Satakarni I performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice and proclaimed himself Lord of the Southern Sea (Dakshinapathapati).

chronicle.era: c. 78 – 130 CE: Gautamiputra Satakarni & the Saka Wars
chronicle.narrative: The zenith of Satavahana power was achieved under Gautamiputra Satakarni (r. c. 106–130 CE), who annihilated the Kshaharata Saka dynasty of Nahapana, counter-striking his coins in the Jogalthambi hoard and restoring the religious and territorial sovereignty of the Deccan from Gujarat to Malwa and Krishna river.

chronicle.era: c. 130 – 225 CE: Vashishtiputra Pulumavi & Maritime Trade
chronicle.narrative: Successors Vashishtiputra Pulumavi and Yajna Sri Satakarni minted coins featuring two-masted seafaring ships, demonstrating thriving oceanic commerce with the Roman Empire as documented in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.

primary_sources.source_title: Nāsik Cave 3 Inscription of Gautami Balaśrī (Year 19 of Vāsiṣṭhīputra Puḷumāvi)
primary_sources.original_text: सक-यवन-पल्हव-निसूदनस खखरात-वस-निरवसेस-करस सातवाहन-कुल-यस-पतिठापन-करस... खतिय-दप-मान-मदनस एक-बम्हणस सिरि-गोतमिपुतस सातकणिस...
primary_sources.transliteration: Saka-Yavana-Palhava-nisūdanasa Khakharāta-vasa-niravasesa-karasa Sātavāhana-kula-yasa-patiṭhāpana-karasa... Khatiya-dapa-māna-madanasa eka-bamhaṇasa siri-Gotamiputasa Sātakaṇisa...
primary_sources.translation: Of the glorious Gautamiputra Satakarni, who crushed the pride of the Sakas, Yavanas, and Pahlavas; who eradicated the race of the Khaharata (Nahapana); who restored the glory of the Satavahana dynasty; who humbled the pride and arrogance of the Kshatriyas; the Unique Brahmana (Eka-Brahmana)... whose war steeds drank the waters of the three oceans (Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana).
primary_sources.academic_citation: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. VIII, pp. 60–65; Sudhakar Chattopadhyaya, The Sakas in India, Visva-Bharati, 1967, pp. 45–52.
primary_sources.significance: The primary royal eulogy detailing the complete geopolitical destruction of the Western Kshatrapas and the trans-oceanic domain of the Satavahana kingdom.

primary_sources.source_title: Junāgaḍh Rock Inscription of Rudradāman I (Girnar, Gujarat)
primary_sources.original_text: दक्षिणापथ-पतेः सातकर्णेर् द्विरपि निर्व्याजम् अवजीत्यावजीत्य संबन्ध-विदूरताया अनुत्सादनात् प्राप्त-यशसा...
primary_sources.transliteration: Dakṣiṇāpatha-pateḥ Sātakarṇer dvir-api nirvjyājam avajītyāvajītya saṁbandha-vidūratāyā anutsādanāt prāpta-yaśasā...
primary_sources.translation: Who, having twice in fair combat completely defeated Satakarni, the Lord of the Deccan (Dakshinapathapati), did not destroy him on account of the non-distant family relationship between them, and thereby gained great fame...
primary_sources.academic_citation: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. VIII, pp. 36–49; D.C. Sircar, Select Inscriptions, Vol. I, pp. 175–186.
primary_sources.significance: The earliest lengthy Sanskrit prose inscription of undisputed date, recording royal diplomatic marriages and boundary wars between the Sakas and Satavahanas.

events.title: Kujula Kadphises Unifies Five Yuezhi Tribes to Found the Kushan Empire
events.desc: Sweeps across the Hindu Kush from Bactria, consolidating Gandhara and Paropamisadae into an agrarian-mercantile power.

shloka.text: नानाश्रान्ताय श्रीरस्तीति रोहित शुश्रुम । पापो नृषद्वरो जन इन्द्र इच्चरतः सखा । चरैवेति चरैवेति ॥
shloka.transliteration: nānāśrāntāya śrīrastīti rohita śuśruma | pāpo nṛṣadvaro jana indra iccarataḥ sakhā | caraiveti caraiveti ||
shloka.translation: Fortune never favors one who refuses to strive forward; Indra himself befriends the tireless explorer—therefore march onward, march onward!

events.title: Vima Kadphises Introduces Imperial Gold Dinar Coinage & Maheshvara Titles
events.desc: Strikes high-purity gold dinaras calibrated to Roman aurei standards, linking Silk Road bullion directly to Gujarat seaports.

shloka.text: प्रजासुखे सुखं राज्ञः प्रजानां च हिते हितम् । नात्मप्रियं हितं राज्ञः प्रजानां तु प्रियं हितम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: prajāsukhe sukhaṁ rājñaḥ prajānāṁ ca hite hitam | nātmapriyaṁ hitaṁ rājñaḥ prajānāṁ tu priyaṁ hitam ||
shloka.translation: In the happiness of the subjects lies the happiness of the sovereign; in their welfare rests his own welfare. Not what pleases himself, but what uplifts his people is the king's good.

events.title: Accession of Kanishka the Great & Inauguration of the Saka/Kanishka Era
events.desc: Establishes an enduring regnal epoch from twin capitals at Purushapura (winter) and Mathura (summer), uniting Northern India and Bactria.

shloka.text: महाराजो राजातिराजो देवपुत्रो कणिष्को ॥ ...काणिक्‍य सम्राजेण साकेतं कौशाम्बीं पाटलिपुत्रं चम्पां च एकराज्याय विजिता ॥
shloka.transliteration: Mahārājo Rājātirājo Devaputro Kaṇiṣko || (...kāṇiṣkasya Sāketaṁ Kauśāmbīṁ Pāṭaliputraṁ Campāṁ ca ekasāmrājye)
shloka.translation: Great King, King of Kings, Son of Heaven Kanishka—recorded across the Mathura royal sanctuary and Bactrian Rabatak charter reaching from Bactria down to Saketa, Kaushambi, Pataliputra, and Champa.
shloka.citation: Māt Kaniṣka Statue Inscription & Rabatak Charter (c. 127–130 CE)

events.title: Rabatak Bactrian Charter Lists Kushan Rule down to Pataliputra & Champa
events.desc: Bactrian-script temple charter confirms Kanishka's direct imperial authority over Saketa, Kaushambi, Pataliputra, and Sri Champa.

shloka.text: देशः पृथिवी । तस्यां हिमवत्-समुद्र-अन्तरं उदीचीनं योजन-सहस्र-परिमाणं तिर्यक्चक्रवर्ति-क्षेत्रम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: deśaḥ pṛthivī | tasyāṁ himavat-samudra-antaraṁ udīcīnaṁ yojana-sahasra-parimāṇaṁ tiryak-cakravarti-kṣetram ||
shloka.translation: The land spanning northward from the Southern Ocean to the snowy Himalayas, measuring a thousand yojanas across, is the imperial Chakravartin domain.

events.title: Charaka Redacts the Caraka Saṁhitā at the Kushan Imperial Court
events.desc: Royal physician Charaka systematizes classical Ayurveda pharmacology, clinical diagnostics, and humoral physiology in Sanskrit.

shloka.text: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः । सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु मा कश्चिद्दुःखभाग्भवेत् ॥
shloka.transliteration: sarve bhavantu sukhinaḥ sarve santu nirāmayāḥ | sarve bhadrāṇi paśyantu mā kaścidduḥkhabhāgbhavet ||
shloka.translation: May all beings dwell in happiness; may all live free from infirmity; may every citizen witness auspicious prosperity, and let none endure sorrow.

events.title: Fourth Buddhist Council Convened at Kundalvana (Kashmir)
events.desc: Guided by Vasumitra and poet Ashvaghosha, 500 scholars compile the Mahavibhasha commentaries and launch Mahayana across Silk Roads.

shloka.text: नुदन्निदाघं जितचारुचन्द्रमाः स वन्द्यतेऽर्हन्निह यस्य नोपमा । आसीद्विशालोन्नतसानुलक्ष्म्या पयोदपङ्क्त्येव परीतपार्श्वम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: nudannidāghaṁ jitacārucandramāḥ sa vandyate'rhanniha yasya nopamā | āsīdviśālonnatasānulakṣmyā payodapaṅktyeva parītapārśvam ||
shloka.translation: Revered is that peerless Awakened One whose cool radiance surpasses the moon, whose Dharma arose beside lofty snowy peaks.

events.title: Ashvaghosha Composes Buddhacarita—Earliest Extant Sanskrit Mahakavya
events.desc: Transforms the life of Gautama Buddha into sublime classical Sanskrit poetry at Kanishka's multi-lingual court.

shloka.text: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वतोऽदब्धासो अपरीतास उद्भिदः ।
shloka.transliteration: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvato 'dabdhāso aparītāsa udbhidaḥ |
shloka.translation: Let noble thoughts and enlightening wisdom come to us from every quarter of the earth, unhindered and illuminating all.

events.title: Twin Flowering of Gandhara Schist & Mathura Red-Sandstone Buddha Sculptures
events.desc: For the first time, ateliers in Peshawar and Mathura sculpt full anthropomorphic images of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas.

shloka.text: अयं निजः परो वेति गणना लघुचेतसाम् । उदारचरितानां तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: ayaṁ nijaḥ paro veti gaṇanā laghucetasām | udāracaritānāṁ tu vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam ||
shloka.translation: 'This one is my kin, that one is a foreigner'—such reckonings belong to small-minded folk; to the noble-hearted, the entire earth is one shared family.

events.title: Erection of the Colossal Kanishka Stupa & Reliquary in Peshawar
events.desc: Towering multi-tiered wooden-and-stone pagoda celebrated by Chinese pilgrims Faxian and Xuanzang as one of Asia's grandest wonders.

shloka.text: चरथ, भिक्खवे, चारिकं बहुजनहिताय बहुजनसुखाय लोकानुकम्पाय अत्थाय हिताय सुखाय देवमनुस्सानं ॥
shloka.transliteration: Caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṁ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ ||
shloka.translation: Walk forth, O monks, upon the wandering mission for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world.

events.title: Reign of Huvishka & Vasudeva I—Synthesizing Shaiva & Buddhist Patronage
events.desc: Mathura sanctuary inscriptions and gold issues honor Shiva (Oesho), Karttikeya, Buddha, Nana, and Helios harmoniously.

shloka.text: देवानंपियो पियदसि राजा सवपासंडानि पूजयति पवजितानि च घरथानि च... सवपासंडानां तु साल-वढी अस ति ॥
shloka.transliteration: Devānaṁpiyo Piyadasi rājā savapāsaṇḍāni pūjayati pavajitāni ca gharathāni ca... savapāsaṇḍānāṁ tu sāla-vaḍhī asa ti ||
shloka.translation: King Priyadarsin honors all religious sects, both ascetics and householders, through gifts and reverence; for the growth of the essential core of every tradition is our true goal.

events.title: Sasanian Pressure & Rise of the Yaudheya Republics & Guptas
events.desc: Indigenous northern republics reassert autonomy in Punjab–Rajasthan while eastern Kushan realms integrate with the Guptas.

shloka.text: परिवर्तिनि संसारे मृतः को वा न जायते । स जातो येन जातेन याति वंशः समुन्नतिम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: parivartini saṁsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate | sa jāto yena jātena yāti vaṁśaḥ samunnatim ||
shloka.translation: In this revolving world, who is not born and does not perish? Truly born is he alone through whose deeds his dynasty and civilization ascend to enduring greatness.

shloka_epigraph.text: φαονανφαο κανOffκε κοφανο... ινα βογοστο καραλραγγο... ογε ινα αβο ιαδο αστα καρανο βαγο λαδο φρεσταδο... οδο ματυρα οδο σιδο σαγητο οδο ζοοβο καοσαμβο οδο παταλιποτρο ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "The king of kings, Kanishka the Kushan... issued an edict in Greek and then put it into the Aryan language... and submitted to his will the realm of India: Champa, Saketa, Kaushambi, and Pataliputra as far as Sri Champa."
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Nicholas Sims-Williams & Joe Cribb, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 4, 1996, pp. 75–142

sources.title: History of Civilizations of Central Asia, Vol. II
sources.author: Janos Harmatta

empires.historical_map_title: The Crossroads Empire — India under the Kushans (c. 30–375 CE)

detailed_history.overview: Arising from the Yuezhi confederacy in Bactria, the Kushan Empire (c. 30–375 CE) created a colossal bridge between the Greco-Roman Mediterranean, the Silk Road of Central Asia, and the fertile Gangetic basin of India. Ruling from twin seasonal capitals at Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura, the Kushans reached their zenith under Kanishka the Great (r. c. 127–150 CE), patronizing the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir and pioneering Mahayana and Gandharan sculpture.

chronicle.era: c. 30 – 127 CE: Kujula & Vima Kadphises
chronicle.narrative: Kujula Kadphises united the five Yuezhi yabghus in the Oxus valley, capturing Gandhara and Taxila. His successor Vima Kadphises introduced high-purity gold dinar coinage struck to the Roman aureus weight standard, identifying himself on coins as an ardent devotee of Lord Shiva (Maheshvara).

chronicle.era: c. 127 – 150 CE: Kanishka the Great & the Golden Climax
chronicle.narrative: Kanishka I inaugurated the Saka / Kanishka Era of 127 CE. The discovery of the Rabatak Inscription in Bactrian confirms his direct rule extended from modern Afghanistan across northern India to Saketa, Kausambi, Pataliputra, and Champa. Kanishka convened the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir under Vasumitra and Ashvaghosha, compiling the Mahavibhasha encyclopedic commentaries.

chronicle.era: c. 150 – 375 CE: Huvishka, Vasudeva I & Sasanian Pressure
chronicle.narrative: Under Huvishka and Vasudeva I, Mathura flourished as a center of Indian sculptural art, crafting colossal images of the Buddha and Hindu deities. The empire gradually contracted in the 3rd century under incursions from the Sasanian Kushano-Shah kings in the west and the rising Republics (Yaudheyas, Malavas) and Guptas in the east.

primary_sources.source_title: Rabatak Inscription of Kanishka I (Baghlan, Afghanistan)
primary_sources.original_text: ...καὶ ἐξήνεγκε χρονικὸν ἰαονανο εἰς ἀριαο... καὶ ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ ἐκράτησε τῆς Ἰνδικῆς· εἰς Κοοαδηνο καὶ εἰς Ὀζηνο καὶ εἰς Ζαγηδο καὶ εἰς Κοζαμβο καὶ εἰς Παλαβοτρο ἕως εἰς Σιριταμπο...
primary_sources.transliteration: ...kai exēnenke chronikon iaonano eis ariao... kai hyper autou ekratēse tēs Indikēs: eis Kooadēno kai eis Ozēno kai eis Zagēdo kai eis Kozambo kai eis Palabotro heōs eis Siritampo...
primary_sources.translation: ...and he inaugurated the year one; and the Greek edict was replaced by the Aryan (Bactrian) tongue... and in India he brought under his dominion: Kundina, Ujjayini, Saketa, Kaushambi, Pataliputra, and as far as Champa; and whatever kings were therein he made subject to his will...
primary_sources.academic_citation: Nicholas Sims-Williams and Joe Cribb, "A New Bactrian Inscription of Kanishka the Great", Silk Road Art and Archaeology 4, 1996, pp. 75–142; B.N. Mukherjee, The Great Kushana Testament, Calcutta, 1998.
primary_sources.significance: The single most decisive epigraph of ancient Central and South Asian history, proving Kanishka's political annexation of Gangetic India down to Pataliputra and Champa.

primary_sources.source_title: Māt Kaniṣka Statue Inscription (Mathura Museum)
primary_sources.original_text: महाराजो राजातिराजो देवपुत्रो कणिष्को ॥
primary_sources.transliteration: Mahārājo Rājātirājo Devaputro Kaṇiṣko ||
primary_sources.translation: The Great King, King of Kings, Son of Heaven, Kanishka.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Heinrich Lüders, Mathura Inscriptions, Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht, 1961, pp. 134–138; J.Ph. Vogel, Catalogue of the Archaeological Museum at Mathura, 1910.
primary_sources.significance: Carved on the base of the colossal headless sandstone statue of Kanishka in Persian tunics and boots at the royal dynastic sanctuary (Devakula) of Mat.

battles.name: Battle of Sondani
battles.parties: Yashodharman of Malwa & Narasimhagupta Baladitya vs. Mihirakula
battles.summary: Decisive victory shattering the Alchon Hun invasion. The cruel tyrant Mihirakula bowed his head before Yashodharman, breaking Hun power in India forever.
battles.source: Mandasor Pillar Inscription of Yashodharman & Xuanzang's Records

events.title: Chandragupta I Assumes Maharajadhiraja & Launches the Gupta Era
events.desc: Forges a strategic marital union with the Licchavi republic of Vaishali, minted on gold dinaras celebrating 'Kumaradevi & Sri Chandragupta'.

shloka.text: उत्तरं यत्समुद्रस्य हिमाद्रेश्चैव दक्षिणम् । वर्षं तद्भारतं नाम भारती यत्र सन्ततिः ॥
shloka.transliteration: uttaraṁ yatsamudrasya himādreścaiva dakṣiṇam | varṣaṁ tadbhārataṁ nāma bhāratī yatra santatiḥ ||
shloka.translation: The sacred expanse lying north of the ocean and south of the snowy Himalayas is named Bharatam; there flourish the descendants of Bharata.

events.title: Samudragupta's Aryavarta & Dakshinapatha Campaigns (Prayag Prashasti)
events.desc: Harishena engraves 33 Sanskrit prose-and-verse lines on the Allahabad Ashokan Pillar detailing conquests from Nepal to Kanchipuram.

shloka.text: सर्व-राजोच्छेत्तुः पृथिव्यामप्रतिरथस्य... सर्वदक्षिणपथराज-ग्रहण-मोक्षानुग्रह-जनितप्रताप-मिश्र-महाभाग्यस्य ॥
shloka.transliteration: sarva-rājocchettuḥ pṛthivyām-apratirathasya... sarva-Dakṣiṇāpatharāja-grahaṇa-mokṣānugraha-janita-pratāpa-miśra-mahābhāgyasya ||
shloka.translation: Of Emperor Samudragupta—without peer upon the earth, conqueror of Aryavarta, whose noble glory shone in capturing, releasing, and restoring the kings of the South in magnanimous sovereignty.
shloka.citation: Allāhābād Pillar Praśasti of Samudragupta (Hariṣeṇa, c. 370 CE)

events.title: Samudragupta Performs Imperial Ashvamedha & Patronizes Vasubandhu
events.desc: Restores classical Ashvamedha gold coinage while celebrating scholarship, Sanskrit kavya, and veena music at court.

shloka.text: वङ्गानुत्खाय तरसा नेता नौसाधनोद्धतान् । निचखान जयस्तम्भान्गङ्गास्रोतोऽन्तरेषु सः ॥
shloka.transliteration: vaṅgānutkhāya tarasā netā nausādhanoddhatān | nicakhāna jayastambhāngaṅgāsroto'ntareṣu saḥ ||
shloka.translation: Having swiftly overcome the naval forces of Vanga, the imperial leader planted towering pillars of victory amidst the deltaic islands of the sacred Ganga.

events.title: Chandragupta II Eliminates the Western Kshatrapas & Takes Vikramaditya
events.desc: Annihilates Rudrasimha III to annex Malwa, Gujarat, and Barygaza, establishing Ujjayini as second imperial capital.

shloka.text: यथा प्रह्लादनाच्चन्द्रः प्रतापात्तपनो यथा । तथैव सोऽभूदन्वर्थो राजा प्रकृतिरञ्जनात् ॥
shloka.transliteration: yathā prahlādanāc-candraḥ pratāpāt-tapano yathā | tathaiva so'bhūd-anvartho rājā prakṛti-rañjanāt ||
shloka.translation: Just as the moon delights by its cool radiance and the sun shines by majestic brilliance, the monarch proved true to the very name 'Raja' by endearing himself to all subjects.

events.title: Creation of the Rust-Free Iron Pillar of Delhi & Udayagiri Caves
events.desc: Metallurgists forge a 6-ton pure wrought iron pillar impervious to corrosion at Mehrauli honoring King Chandra.

shloka.text: यस्योद्वर्तयतः प्रतीपमुरसा शत्रून्समेत्यागतान् वङ्गेष्वाहववर्तिनोऽभिलिखिता खड्गेन कीर्तिर्भुजे । तीर्त्वा सप्त मुखानि येन समरे सिन्धोर्जिता बाह्लिकाः ॥
shloka.transliteration: yasyodvartayataḥ pratīpam-urasā śatrūn sametyāgatān vaṅgeṣv-āhava-vartino'bhilikhitā khaḍgena kīrtirbhuje | tīrtvā sapta mukhāni yena samare sindhorjitā bāhlikāḥ ||
shloka.translation: Whose fame was inscribed by the sword in Vanga when enemies united against him, and who crossed the seven mouths of the Indus in warfare to vanquish Bactria—King Chandra Vikramaditya.
shloka.citation: Mehrauli Iron Pillar Inscription of King Chandra (c. 400 CE)

events.title: Pilgrimage of Faxian & Literary Zenith of Poet Kalidasa
events.desc: Chinese traveler Faxian records prosperous, lenient governance without capital punishment while Kalidasa composes Shakuntala, Meghaduta, and Raghuvamsha.

shloka.text: वागर्थाविव सम्पृक्तौ वागर्थप्रतिपत्तये । जगतः पितरौ वन्दे पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ ॥
shloka.transliteration: vāgarthāviva sampṛktau vāgarthapratipattaye | jagataḥ pitarau vande pārvatīparameśvarau ||
shloka.translation: Inseparable as word and its meaning, I bow to Parvati and Parameshvara, the eternal parents of the cosmos, for illumination in eloquence and truth.

events.title: Kumaragupta I Founds Nalanda Mahavihara Residential University
events.desc: Endows the monastic university at Nalanda that soon draws 10,000 scholars across India, Tibet, Korea, China, and Southeast Asia.

shloka.text: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
shloka.transliteration: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṁ pavitramiha vidyate |
shloka.translation: In all this world there exists no purifier equal to luminous knowledge and scholarly inquiry.

events.title: Skandagupta Repulses Pushyamitra & Huna Armies; Restores Sudarshana Dam
events.desc: Bhitari and Junagadh inscriptions celebrate his defense of the borders and engineering triumph rebuilding Gujarat's burst dam in sixty days.

shloka.text: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् । दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: śauryaṁ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṁ yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam | dānam īśvara-bhāvaś ca kṣātraṁ karma svabhāva-jam ||
shloka.translation: Valor, splendor, steadfast resolve, tactical skill, refusing flight in battle, generosity, and noble leadership are the innate duties of sovereign guardians.

events.title: Aryabhata Completes the Āryabhaṭīya at Kusumapura (Pataliputra)
events.desc: Calculates pi = 3.1416, sine tables, solar year length, Earth's axial rotation, and eclipse mechanics at age twenty-three.

shloka.text: चतुराधिकं शतमष्टगुणं द्वाषष्टिस्तथा सहस्राणाम् । अयुतद्वयस्य विष्कम्भस्यासन्नो वृत्तपरिणाहः ॥
shloka.transliteration: caturādhikaṁ śatamaṣṭaguṇaṁ dvāṣaṣṭistathā sahasrāṇām | ayutadvayasya viṣkambhasyāsanno vṛttapariṇāhaḥ ||
shloka.translation: Add 4 to 100, multiply by 8, and add 62,000: by this rule the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 20,000 is closely 62,832 (yielding pi = 3.1416).

events.title: Classical Temple Genesis at Deogarh Dashavatara & Ajanta Cave Viharas
events.desc: Architects pioneer Nagara stone shikhara sanctums at Deogarh while Vakataka–Gupta painters illuminate Ajanta.

shloka.text: आर्यभटस्त्रीणि गदति गणितं कालक्रियां गोलम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: Āryabhaṭastrīṇi gadati gaṇitaṁ kālakriyāṁ golam ||
shloka.translation: Aryabhata expounds in clarity the three twin sciences: Mathematics (Ganita), Reckoning of Celestial Time (Kalakriya), and the Spherical Cosmos (Gola).

events.title: Battle of Sondani: Yashodharman & Narasimhagupta Crush Mihirakula
events.desc: Decisive coalition triumph expels the Alchon Huns from central and northern India, recorded on twin victory pillars at Mandasor.

shloka.text: उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः । न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः ॥
shloka.transliteration: udyamena hi sidhyanti kāryāṇi na manorathaiḥ | na hi suptasya siṁhasya praviśanti mukhe mṛgāḥ ||
shloka.translation: Tasks are accomplished solely through resolute exertion, never through passive wishes; prey never walks of its own accord into a sleeping lion's mouth.

events.title: Varahamihira's Bṛhat Saṁhitā & Transition to Post-Gupta Kingdoms
events.desc: Encyclopedic synthesis of astronomy, architecture, botany, and hydrology crowns the twilight of the imperial Gupta age.

shloka.text: विद्वत्वं च नृपत्वं च नैव तुल्यं कदाचन । स्वदेशे पूज्यते राजा विद्वान् सर्वत्र पूज्यते ॥
shloka.transliteration: vidvatvaṁ ca nṛpatvaṁ ca naiva tulyaṁ kadācana | svadeśe pūjyate rājā vidvān sarvatra pūjyate ||
shloka.translation: Scholarship and royalty can never be equated: a king is honored only within his own realm, whereas the scholar is revered throughout the world.

shloka_epigraph.text:
यस्य प्रज्ञानुषङ्गोचितसुखमनसः शास्त्रतत्त्वार्थभर्तुः
स्तब्धो नीचैः प्रसिद्धो बुधगुणकविभिः कीर्तिमान् राजराजः ।
सर्वपृथिवीविजयजनितोदयव्याप्तनिखिलभुवनस्य
सुचरितचरितानुबद्धावदातमतेः श्रीसमुद्रगुप्तस्य ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "Whose mind was filled with joy through constant communion with wisdom; who was the patron of the true spirit of the scriptures; whose famous title was King of Kings (Rajaraja); who conquered the entire earth and whose fame filled all the worlds; whose intellect was purified by virtuous conduct — Sri Samudragupta."
shloka_epigraph.citation: Allahabad Stone Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti) composed by Court Poet Harishena
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum (CII), Vol. III: Inscriptions of the Early Gupta Kings (J.F. Fleet, 1888, pp. 1–17)

sources.title: The Classical Age (The History and Culture of the Indian People, Vol. III)
sources.author: R.C. Majumdar (ed.)

empires.historical_map_title: India in the Gupta Golden Age (c. 320–550 CE)

detailed_history.overview: The Imperial Guptas (c. 319–550 CE) established the Classical Golden Age of ancient India from their metropolitan capital at Pataliputra. Re-unifying northern India and exercising tributary suzerainty over the Deccan and northwestern frontiers, the era witnessed unprecedented advances in mathematics (Aryabhata's zero and trigonometry), metallurgy (the rustless Iron Pillar of Delhi), classical Sanskrit literature (Kalidasa), and monumental rock architecture (Ajanta and Udayagiri).

chronicle.era: c. 319 – 335 CE: Chandragupta I & the Licchavi Alliance
chronicle.narrative: Chandragupta I assumed the imperial title Maharajadhiraja (King of Kings) and established the Gupta Era in 319 CE. His diplomatic marriage to princess Kumaradevi of the ancient Licchavi clan was celebrated on gold coins, uniting the economic and moral resources of Magadha and northern Bihar.

chronicle.era: c. 335 – 375 CE: Samudragupta & the Imperial Digvijaya
chronicle.narrative: Described by historian Vincent Smith as the 'Napoleon of India', Samudragupta conducted comprehensive military campaigns recorded in the Prayag Prashasti on the Ashoka pillar in Allahabad. He exterminated nine kings of Aryavarta (Northern India), captured and liberated twelve kings of Dakshinapatha (Peninsular India as far south as Kanchipuram), and received tribute from frontier rulers (Samatata, Kamarupa, Nepal, Kartripura) and the Kushano-Sasanian Daivaputras.

chronicle.era: c. 375 – 455 CE: Chandragupta II Vikramaditya & Golden Zenith
chronicle.narrative: Chandragupta II eliminated the Western Kshatrapas of Gujarat and Saurashtra, securing western maritime ports (Bharuch, Cambay). He established a secondary capital at Ujjayini and patronized the Navaratnas (Nine Gems of scholarship, including poet Kalidasa and astronomer Varahamihira). His daughter Prabhavatigupta served as regent of the powerful Vakataka kingdom in the Deccan.

chronicle.era: c. 455 – 550 CE: Skandagupta & the Huna Invasions
chronicle.narrative: Kumaragupta I founded the monastic university of Nalanda. Upon his death, Skandagupta successfully repelled catastrophic invasions by the White Hunas (Hephthalites) as commemorated on the Bhitari stone pillar, but prolonged defense drained imperial reserves, leading to gradual decentralization into regional successor kingdoms.

primary_sources.source_title: Allāhābād Pillar Inscription / Prayāga Praśasti of Samudragupta (by Court Poet Hariṣeṇa)
primary_sources.original_text: सर्व-राजोच्छेत्तुः पृथिव्यामप्रतिरथस्य... कौशलक-माहेन्द्र-महाकान्तारक-व्याघ्रराज-कौरालकमण्टराज-पैष्टपुरक-महेन्द्रगिरि... काञ्चेयक-विष्णुगोपावमुक्तक-नीलराज-वैवेयक-हस्तिवर्मन्-पालक्कोग्रसेन... कौस्थलपुरक-धनञ्जय प्रभृति-सर्व-दक्षिणपथ-राज-ग्रहण-मोक्षानुग्रह-जनित-महाभाग्यस्य...
primary_sources.transliteration: Sarva-rājocchettuḥ pṛthivyām-apratirathasya... Kauśalaka-Māhendra-Māhākāntāraka-Vyāghrarāja-Kaurālaka-Maṇṭarāja-Paiṣṭapuraka-Mahendragiri... Kāñceyaka-Viṣṇugopāvamuktaka-Nīlarāja-Vaiveyaka-Hastivarman-Pālakkograsena... Kausthalapuraka-Dhanañjaya prabhṛti-sarva-Dakṣiṇapatha-rāja-grahaṇa-mokṣānugraha-janita-mahābhāgyasya...
primary_sources.translation: Of the Exterminator of all kings, who had no counterpart on earth... whose great glory arose from capturing, liberating, and bestowing royal favor upon all the kings of the Southern Country (Dakshinapatha)—such as Mahendra of Kosala, Vyaghraraja of Mahakantara, Mahendragiri of Pishtapura, Vishnugopa of Kanchi, Hastivarman of Vengi, and Ugrasena of Palakka... who exterminated the kings of Aryavarta... and received personal submission and tribute from the Daivaputras, Shahis, Shahanushahis, Sakas, and the dwellers of Simhala (Sri Lanka).
primary_sources.academic_citation: J.F. Fleet, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. III: Inscriptions of the Early Gupta Kings and Their Successors, Calcutta, 1888, pp. 1–17; D.C. Sircar, Select Inscriptions, Vol. I, pp. 262–270.
primary_sources.significance: The master epigraphic panegyric of ancient Indian statecraft, establishing the distinction between direct annexation in northern India and tributary protectorates in peninsular India.

primary_sources.source_title: Mehrauli Iron Pillar Inscription of King Candra (Qutb Complex, Delhi)
primary_sources.original_text: यस्योद्वर्तयतः प्रतीपमुरसा शत्रून्समेत्यागतान् वङ्गेष्वाहववर्तिनोऽभिलिखिता खड्गेन कीर्तिर्भुजे । तीर्त्वा सप्त मुखानि येन समरे सिन्धोर्जिता बाह्लिका...
primary_sources.transliteration: Yasyodvartayataḥ pratīpam-urasā śatrūn-sametyāgatān vaṅgeṣvāhava-vartino'bhilikhitā khaḍgena kīrtir-bhuje | Tīrtvā sapta mukhāni yena samare sindhor-jitā bāhlikā...
primary_sources.translation: By him, on whose arm fame was inscribed by the sword when in the Vanga countries (Bengal) he kneaded back with his breast the enemies who had united and stood against him; by whom, having crossed in warfare the seven mouths of the river Indus, the Vahlikas (Bactria) were vanquished; by the breezes of whose prowess the southern ocean is even still perfumed...
primary_sources.academic_citation: J.F. Fleet, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. III, pp. 139–142; R. Balasubramaniam, Delhi Iron Pillar: New Insights, Indian Institute of Advanced Study, Shimla, 2002.
primary_sources.significance: Celebrates the trans-continental military expeditions of King Chandra (identified with Chandragupta II Vikramaditya) on an uncorroded 6-ton pure wrought iron monument.

locations.name: Pataliputra
locations.role: Imperial seat of the Guptas in Magadha
locations.desc: Sprawling capital celebrated by Chinese traveler Faxian for its lavish charitable hospitals and monasteries.

locations.name: Ujjayini
locations.role: Second imperial capital under Chandragupta II Vikramaditya
locations.desc: Cultural capital where the Nine Jewels (Navaratnas) including poet-dramatist Kalidasa assembled.

locations.name: Prayaga (Allahabad)
locations.role: Confluence of Ganga-Yamuna; site of Harishena's Allahabad Pillar Inscription
locations.desc: Monolithic Ashokan pillar engraved with Harishena's 33-line Sanskrit prasasti of Samudragupta's conquests.

locations.name: Nalanda
locations.role: Pan-Asian residential university founded by Kumaragupta I
locations.desc: Premier international center of learning housing over 10,000 scholars from across Asia.

locations.name: Vidisha / Udayagiri
locations.role: Malwa administrative center and cave sanctuary
locations.desc: Udayagiri Cave 5 features the monumental rock-cut Varaha rescuing the Earth Goddess, commissioned under Chandragupta II.

locations.name: Eran (Airikina)
locations.role: Military base of Samudragupta and Bhanugupta
locations.desc: Famous for the colossal Varaha statue, Janardana temple, and the 510 CE Goparaja Sati pillar.

locations.name: Mathura
locations.role: Center of Classical Gupta sculpture and religious harmony
locations.desc: Created the serene standing Buddha statues with wet-drapery folds that defined classical Asian iconography.

locations.name: Tamralipti
locations.role: Foremost eastern seaport trading with Southeast Asia and China
locations.desc: Where Faxian spent two years copying Buddhist sutras before embarking for Sri Lanka.

locations.name: Valabhi
locations.role: Western administrative center in Saurashtra under the Maitrakas
locations.desc: Renowned for higher learning, Buddhist viharas, and the codification of the Jaina canonical agamas.

locations.name: Bhitari
locations.role: Royal pillar inscription documenting Skandagupta's defense against Hunas
locations.desc: Skandagupta's red sandstone monolithic pillar recounting his sleepless battle against the barbarian hordes.

locations.name: Deogarh (Dashavatara Temple)
locations.role: Masterpiece of Gupta panchayatana temple architecture
locations.desc: Classic 6th-century stone temple featuring the reclining Sheshashayi Vishnu sculpture on the Betwa river.

locations.name: Kanchipuram
locations.role: Southernmost point reached in Samudragupta's Digvijaya
locations.desc: King Vishnugopa of Kanchi was defeated and restored as a tributary ally.

empires.name: Vardhana Empire of Harsha

capitals.name: Kannauj (Kanyakubja)
capitals.role: Imperial seat of Emperor Harsha; glorious metropolis of the Ganga
capitals.desc: Multi-walled city with hundreds of Buddhist monasteries and Hindu temples described by Xuanzang.

capitals.name: Thanesar (Sthanishvara)
capitals.role: Ancestral Vardhana dynastic capital in Kurukshetra
capitals.desc: Seat of King Prabhakaravardhana and birthplace of Harsha along the sacred Saraswati river.

boundary_phases.description: Young Harsha unifies Thanesar and Maukhari Kannauj, rescuing Queen Rajyashri and launching his eastern campaign.
Sovereign northern empire spanning from Punjab and Vallabhi to Magadha, Bengal, Kongoda (Odisha), with Kamarupa alliance.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Chalukya Empire of Badami (Pulakeshin II)
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Badami Chalukya empire under Pulakeshin II; dominant power across the Deccan and Narmada.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Kamarupa (King Bhaskaravarman)
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Ancient kingdom in the Brahmaputra valley (Assam) ruled by King Bhaskaravarman, close ally of Emperor Harsha.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Pallava Dynasty
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Dravidian dynasty of Kanchipuram; maritime expeditions to Southeast Asia and monolithic shore temples at Mamallapuram.

battles.name: Battle of the Narmada River
battles.parties: Harsha (Lord of the North) vs. Pulakeshin II Chalukya (Lord of the South)
battles.summary: Clash of the Titans. Harsha led his vast northern host with thousands of elephants to the Narmada; Pulakeshin's disciplined Deccan army repelled the invasion, establishing the river as the permanent imperial boundary.
battles.source: Aihole Inscription of Pulakeshin II, Verse 23 & Xuanzang's Records

battles.name: Harsha's War with Shashanka of Gauda
battles.parties: Harsha & Bhaskaravarman vs. Shashanka of Gauda (Bengal)
battles.summary: Harsha swore vengeance for the treacherous murder of his brother Rajyavardhana; allied with Kamarupa, he waged protracted campaigns, eventually annexing Bengal after Shashanka's death.

battles.name: Subjugation of Vallabhi
battles.parties: Harsha vs. Dhruvasena II (Maitrakas of Gujarat)
battles.summary: Harsha invaded Saurashtra, defeating Dhruvasena II; with the mediation of Dadda II of Broach, Dhruvasena submitted, married Harsha's daughter, and became a premier feudatory.

battles.name: Conquest of Kongoda (Odisha)
battles.parties: Harsha vs. Sailodbhava Rulers of Kongoda
battles.summary: Harsha's final military campaign, subduing the coastal kingdom of Kongoda along the Bay of Bengal and distributing the revenues among scholars and monks.

battles.name: Rescue of Rajyashri in the Vindhyas
battles.parties: Harsha & Buddhist Monk Divakaramitra vs. Jungle Hostilities
battles.summary: Following the assassination of King Grahavarman of Kannauj, Harsha tracked his widowed sister Rajyashri into the Vindhya forests, rescuing her as she was about to mount a funeral pyre.

battles.name: Campaign against the Hunas of Punjab
battles.parties: Crown Prince Rajyavardhana & Harsha vs. Huna Invaders
battles.summary: King Prabhakaravardhana dispatched his sons to the Himalayan foothills, where Rajyavardhana smashed the Huna horsemen while Harsha hunted in the rear forests.

events.title: Prince Harsha Leads Northwestern Defense Against Alchon Huna Remnants
events.desc: Alongside crown prince Rajyavardhana, sixteen-year-old Harsha campaigns across northern Punjab frontiers.

shloka.text: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् । दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: śauryaṁ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṁ yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam | dānam īśvara-bhāvaś ca kṣātraṁ karma svabhāva-jam ||
shloka.translation: Valor, splendor, steadfast resolve, tactical skill, refusing flight in battle, generosity, and noble leadership are the innate duties of sovereign guardians.

events.title: Tragedy at Kannauj, Rescue in the Vindhyas & Dual Coronation
events.desc: Following murders of Prabhakaravardhana and Rajyavardhana, Harsha rescues sister Rajyashri from Vindhya forests and unites Thanesar & Kannauj.

shloka.text: दैवेनापि क्रियते भव्यानां पूर्वसेवेव । विद्वज्जनसम्पर्को नष्टेष्टज्ञातिदर्शनाभ्युदयः ॥
shloka.transliteration: daivenāpi kriyate bhavyānāṁ pūrvaseveva | vidvajjanasamparko naṣṭeṣṭajñātidarśanābhyudayaḥ ||
shloka.translation: Providence itself serves the noble-souled: granting communion with wise scholars and blissful reunion with beloved kindred restored from adversity.

events.title: Alliance with Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa (Assam) Against Shashanka
events.desc: Receives royal umbrella embassy from Kamarupa envoy Hamsavega along the Sarasvati bank, sealing an enduring eastern frontier pact.

shloka.text: वल्मीकश्च सुमेरुः कृतप्रतिज्ञस्य वीरस्य । धृतधनुषि बाहुशालिनि शैला न नमन्ति यत्तदाश्चर्यम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: valmīkaśca sumeruḥ kṛtapratijñasya vīrasya | dhṛtadhanuṣi bāhuśālini śailā na namanti yattadāścaryam ||
shloka.translation: Even Mount Sumeru appears no taller than an anthill before a resolute hero of iron vow; what wonder when mountains themselves bow before his uplifted bow?

events.title: Battle of the Narmada: Pulakeshin II Halts Harsha's Southern Advance
events.desc: Immortalized in Ravikirti's Aihole Prashasti, Chalukya war elephants fix the Narmada as eternal frontier between North and South India.

shloka.text: अपरिमितविभूतिस्फीतसामन्तसेना-मकुटमणिमयूखाक्रान्तपादारविन्दः । युधि पतितगजेन्द्रानीकबीभत्सभूतो भयविगलितहर्षो येन चाकारि हर्षः ॥
shloka.transliteration: aparimita-vibhūti-sphīta-sāmanta-senā-makuṭa-maṇi-mayūkhākrānta-pādāravindaḥ | yudhi patita-gajendrānīka-bībhatsa-bhūto bhaya-vigalita-harṣo yena cākāri Harṣaḥ ||
shloka.translation: Harsha—whose lotus feet shone with the diadem-jewels of countless vassal hosts—had his joy ('Harsha') dissolved in awe when his mighty war elephants fell upon the Narmada bank before Pulakeshin II.
shloka.citation: Aihole Praśasti of Ravikīrti (Meguti Temple, 634 CE)

events.title: Subjugation & Marital Reconciliation with Vallabhi in Gujarat
events.desc: Defeats Maitraka King Dhruvasena II of Vallabhi, then weds his daughter to the ruler—securing western maritime trade corridors.

shloka.text: स्वराष्ट्रे न्यायवृत्तः स्याद् भृशदण्डश्च शत्रुषु । सुहृत्स्वजिह्मः स्निग्धेषु ब्राह्मणेषु क्षमान्वितः ॥
shloka.transliteration: svarāṣṭre nyāyavṛttaḥ syād bhṛśadaṇḍaśca śatruṣu | suhṛtsvajihmaḥ snigdheṣu brāhmaṇeṣu kṣamānvitaḥ ||
shloka.translation: Within his own kingdom a ruler must uphold strict justice, be formidable against aggressors, unfailingly loyal toward allies, and compassionate toward scholars and citizens.

events.title: Banskhera & Madhuban Royal Copper Plates Signed by Harsha's Own Hand
events.desc: Harsha issues tax-free agrahara endowments bearing his own ornate Siddhamatrika autograph: 'Svahasto mama Maharajadhiraja Sri Harshasya'.

shloka.text: प्रजासुखे सुखं राज्ञः प्रजानां च हिते हितम् । नात्मप्रियं हितं राज्ञः प्रजानां तु प्रियं हितम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: prajāsukhe sukhaṁ rājñaḥ prajānāṁ ca hite hitam | nātmapriyaṁ hitaṁ rājñaḥ prajānāṁ tu priyaṁ hitam ||
shloka.translation: In the happiness of the subjects lies the happiness of the sovereign; in their welfare rests his own welfare. Not what pleases himself, but what uplifts his people is the king's good.

events.title: Pilgrim Xuanzang Travels India & Studies Five Years at Nalanda
events.desc: Master of Law Xuanzang documents thriving monastic hostels, 100-village Nalanda endowments, and Harsha's tireless frontier tours.

shloka.text: विद्वत्वं च नृपत्वं च नैव तुल्यं कदाचन । स्वदेशे पूज्यते राजा विद्वान् सर्वत्र पूज्यते ॥
shloka.transliteration: vidvatvaṁ ca nṛpatvaṁ ca naiva tulyaṁ kadācana | svadeśe pūjyate rājā vidvān sarvatra pūjyate ||
shloka.translation: Scholarship and royalty can never be equated: a king is honored only within his own realm, whereas the scholar is revered throughout the world.

events.title: Harsha Authors Classical Sanskrit Plays Ratnāvalī, Priyadarśikā & Nāgānanda
events.desc: Emperor-dramatist patronizes Banabhatta and composes three enduring plays—two romantic comedies and a Buddhist Bodhisattva drama.

shloka.text: वागर्थाविव सम्पृक्तौ वागर्थप्रतिपत्तये । जगतः पितरौ वन्दे पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ ॥
shloka.transliteration: vāgarthāviva sampṛktau vāgarthapratipattaye | jagataḥ pitarau vande pārvatīparameśvarau ||
shloka.translation: Inseparable as word and its meaning, I bow to Parvati and Parameshvara, the eternal parents of the cosmos, for illumination in eloquence and truth.

events.title: Conquest of Kongoda (Odisha) & Envoy Exchange with Tang Emperor Taizong
events.desc: Consolidates eastern seaboard down to Ganjam while dispatching diplomatic envoys between Kannauj and Tang Chang'an.

shloka.text: अयं निजः परो वेति गणना लघुचेतसाम् । उदारचरितानां तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: ayaṁ nijaḥ paro veti gaṇanā laghucetasām | udāracaritānāṁ tu vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam ||
shloka.translation: 'This one is my kin, that one is a foreigner'—such reckonings belong to small-minded folk; to the noble-hearted, the entire earth is one shared family.

events.title: Grand Kannauj Religious Debate & Prayag Maha-Moksha Parishad
events.desc: Before 20 kings and 5,000 scholars at Kannauj and Prayag, Harsha empties his five-year treasury in universal charity down to his own tunic.

shloka.text: अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् । परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् ॥
shloka.transliteration: aṣṭādaśapurāṇeṣu vyāsasya vacanadvayam | paropakāraḥ puṇyāya pāpāya parapīḍanam ||
shloka.translation: Across all eighteen Puranas, the sage Vyasa distills two eternal maxims: charitable service to others brings sacred merit; inflicting harm upon others brings ruin.
shloka.citation: Subhāṣita / Skanda & Padma Purāṇa Tradition (Prayāg Charity Assembly)

shloka_epigraph.text:
अपरिमितमहिमोपनतसकलसामन्तचूडामणिमयूखवासितचरणयुगलः... परममाहेश्वरो महाराजाधिराज श्रीहर्षः ॥
स्वहस्तो मम महाराजाधिराज श्रीहर्षस्य ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation:
"Whose pair of feet is perfumed by the rays from the crest-jewels of all the feudatory kings who bowed down before his boundless majesty... The supreme devotee of Shiva (Parama-maheshvara), King of Kings, Sri Harsha.
Signed with the own hand of Sri Harsha, King of Kings."
shloka_epigraph.citation: Banskhera Copper Plate Inscription of Harsha, Year 22 (628 CE)
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. IV, pp. 208–211 (G. Buhler)

sources.title: Harsha: A Political and Cultural Study
sources.author: D. Devahuti

empires.historical_map_title: North India in the Age of Harshavardhana (c. 600–650 CE)

detailed_history.overview: Following the collapse of the imperial Guptas, King Harshavardhana (r. 606–647 CE) of the Pushyabhuti dynasty united northern India from his cosmopolitan capital at Kanyakubja (Kannauj). A monarch of celebrated military vigor, artistic refinement (authoring Sanskrit plays Ratnavali, Priyadarsika, and Nagananda), and Buddhist patronage, Harsha's reign was immortalized by court poet Banabhatta in the Harshacharita and Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Xuanzang.

chronicle.era: 606 – 612 CE: Accession & Kannauj Alliance
chronicle.narrative: Ascending the throne of Thanesar at age sixteen following the assassinations of his father Prabhakaravardhana and brother Rajyavardhana by Shashanka of Gauda, Harsha united the crowns of Thanesar and Maukhari Kannauj with his sister Rajyashri.

chronicle.era: 612 – 630 CE: Five Indies Campaigns & Aihole Frontier
chronicle.narrative: Harsha waged continuous campaigns for thirty years across the 'Five Indies' (Punjab, Kannauj, Gauda, Mithila, and Odisha). When attempting to expand south of the Narmada river in c. 618–619 CE, he was repulsed by the Western Chalukya emperor Pulakeshin II, fixing the Narmada as the permanent sovereign border between northern and peninsular India.

chronicle.era: 630 – 647 CE: Xuanzang's Chronicle & The Great Assemblies
chronicle.narrative: In 643 CE, Harsha convened the Kannauj Assembly for religious disputation, attended by 20 kings, 4,000 monks, and Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang. He held the quinquennial Maha-Moksha-Parishad at the sacred confluence in Prayag, where he distributed the accumulated wealth of the royal treasury to ascetics, the poor, and scholars.

primary_sources.source_title: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang), Dà Táng Xīyù Jì (Great Tang Records on the Western Regions)
primary_sources.original_text: 戒日王仁慈好施，凡諸國之賦稅，分為四份：一充國用祭祀，一以封建官屬，一賞聰明才智，一樹福田濟貧... 每五年一設無遮大會，傾竭府庫，以施僧俗貧乏...
primary_sources.transliteration: Jièrì wáng réncí hào shī, fán zhū guó zhī fùshuì, fēn wéi sì fèn: yī chōng guó yòng jìsì, yī yǐ fēngjiàn guānshǔ, yī shǎng cōngmíng cáizhì, yī shù fútián jì pín... Měi wǔ nián yī shè wúzhē dàhuì, qīng jié fǔkù, yǐ shī sēng sú pín fá...
primary_sources.translation: King Shiladitya (Harsha) was of compassionate disposition and liberal in charity. The royal revenues were divided into four portions: one for state affairs and sacrifices, one for the endowment of ministers, one for rewarding intellectual eminence and artists, and one for charity to the needy. Every five years he assembled the Great Arena of Charitable Distribution (Maha-Moksha-Parishad) at Prayag, emptying out the imperial storehouses and giving away gold, gems, and garments until he had given even his own personal vestments and wore a borrowed cloth.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Samuel Beal, Si-Yu-Ki: Buddhist Records of the Western World, Vol. I, Trubner & Co., London, 1884, pp. 210–222; Thomas Watters, On Yuan Chwang's Travels in India, Royal Asiatic Society, 1904.
primary_sources.significance: The paramount foreign documentary account detailing the royal philanthropic governance, economic administration, and Buddhist patron conferences of Harsha.

primary_sources.source_title: Aihole Inscription of Pulakeśin II (by Court Poet Ravikīrti, Meguti Temple)
primary_sources.original_text: अपरिमित-विभूति-स्फीत-सामन्त-सेना-मकुट-मणि-मयूखाक्रान्त-पादारविन्दः । युधि पतित-गजेंद्रानीक-बीभोत्स-भूतो भय-विगलित-हर्षो येन चाकारि हर्षः ॥
primary_sources.transliteration: Aparimita-vibhūti-sphīta-sāmanta-senā-makuṭa-maṇi-mayūkhākrānta-pādāravindaḥ | Yudhi patita-gajendrānīka-bībhotsa-bhūto bhaya-vigalita-harṣo yena cākāri Harṣaḥ ||
primary_sources.translation: Harsha, whose lotus feet were covered with the rays of the jewels of the diadems of hosts of feudatories, and who was endowed with boundless wealth, was caused by Pulakeshin to have his joy (Harsha) melt away in fear, when his array of mighty war elephants was slain in battle on the banks of the Narmada.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. VI, pp. 1–12; K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India, Oxford University Press, 1955.
primary_sources.significance: A rare and brilliant classical Sanskrit pun commemorating the decisive battlefield encounter where peninsular India halted northern imperial expansion.

locations.name: Kannauj (Kanyakubja)
locations.role: Imperial seat of Emperor Harsha; glorious metropolis of the Ganga
locations.desc: Multi-walled city with hundreds of Buddhist monasteries and Hindu temples described by Xuanzang.

locations.name: Thanesar (Sthanishvara)
locations.role: Ancestral Vardhana dynastic capital in Kurukshetra
locations.desc: Seat of King Prabhakaravardhana and birthplace of Harsha along the sacred Saraswati river.

locations.name: Prayag (Allahabad)
locations.role: Site of Harsha's quinquennial Maha Moksha Parishad
locations.desc: Where Harsha held his 75-day festival distributing all royal wealth and personal jewelry to monks and the poor.

locations.name: Nalanda Mahavihara
locations.role: Buddhist international university endowed with 100 villages by Harsha
locations.desc: Xuanzang studied Yogachara doctrine here under Abbot Shilabhadra for five years.

locations.name: Valabhi
locations.role: Maitraka western capital subordinated through dynastic alliance
locations.desc: King Dhruvasena II married Harsha's daughter and attended the grand Kannauj assembly.

locations.name: Varanasi
locations.role: Spiritual center on the Ganga visited by Harsha and Xuanzang
locations.desc: Described by Xuanzang as having 30 Buddhist monasteries and 100 Deva temples with a 100-foot copper statue of Shiva.

locations.name: Mathura
locations.role: Major religious center along the Yamuna in Harsha's realm
locations.desc: Flourishing Buddhist stupas and five grand monasteries along the river banks.

locations.name: Kamarupa (Pragjyotishpura)
locations.role: Allied kingdom of King Bhaskaravarman in Assam
locations.desc: Allied with Harsha to defeat Shashanka of Gauda; escorted Xuanzang to the Kannauj court.

locations.name: Kongoda (Ganjam)
locations.role: Coastal Orissan realm subdued in Harsha's last campaign
locations.desc: Annexed by Harsha in 643 CE, extending his sovereignty to the Chilika Lake.

locations.name: Ahichchhatra
locations.role: Major fortified city in the central province of Harsha
locations.desc: Excavated with monumental terraced temples and Harsha-era seals.

locations.name: Shravasti
locations.role: Historical Kosalan city visited by Xuanzang
locations.desc: Though partially ruined, Jetavana monastery remained an active pilgrimage sanctuary.

locations.name: Tamralipti
locations.role: Eastern seaport connecting Harsha's empire to Southeast Asia and China
locations.desc: Visited by Chinese pilgrim Daoxuan and maritime merchants carrying Buddhist texts.

empires.name: Classical Southern Dynasties: Chola, Chera, Pandya & Pallava
empires.name_hi: दक्षिणसाम्राज्यम्: चोल, चेर, पाण्ड्य, पल्लव एवं चालुक्य
empires.era_type: Maritime Mastery, Dravidian Temple Architecture & Sangam Literature

capitals.name: Thanjavur
capitals.role: Imperial Chola capital; site of Rajaraja's Brihadisvara Temple
capitals.desc: Granary of Tamilakam and administrative seat of the Middle Chola Empire.

capitals.name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram
capitals.role: New imperial capital built by Rajendra Chola I after victorious northern march
capitals.desc: Founded 1025 CE with the vast Cholaganga irrigation reservoir ('Liquid Pillar of Victory').

capitals.name: Madurai
capitals.role: Ancient Pandya capital on the Vaigai river
capitals.desc: Sacred center of the three legendary Tamil Sangam literary assemblies and the Meenakshi temple.

capitals.name: Kanchipuram
capitals.role: Grand Pallava capital and educational center (Ghatika)
capitals.desc: City of a thousand temples; capital of Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I.

capitals.name: Vatapi (Badami)
capitals.role: Rock-cut cliff capital of the Early Western Chalukyas
capitals.desc: Seat of Pulakeshin II surrounded by red sandstone cliff temples and Lake Agastya.

capitals.name: Manyakheta (Malkhed)
capitals.role: Imperial capital of the Rashtrakuta Empire
capitals.desc: Founded by Amoghavarsha I; celebrated by Arab merchant Sulaiman as one of the four great empires of the world.

boundary_phases.phase: Sangam Triarchy: Chola, Chera & Pandya (c. 150 CE)
boundary_phases.description: Classical Tamilakam Muventhar kingdoms ruling from Madurai, Uraiyur, and Vanchi–Muziris with Mediterranean maritime trade.
Pallavas of Kanchi (Mamallapuram sculptors) & Western Chalukyas of Badami contest the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab.

boundary_phases.phase: Imperial Chola Zenith & Trans-Oceanic Thalassocracy (1030 CE)
boundary_phases.description: Under Rajaraja I and Rajendra I: unified South India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, coastal Kalinga–Bengal expedition, and Southeast Asian naval campaigns.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Harsha's Empire (North of Narmada)
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Harsha's Empire (North of Narmada): Contemporaneous frontier realm and trading partner.

neighboring_kingdoms.name: Anuradhapura Kingdom (Sri Lanka)
neighboring_kingdoms.desc: Anuradhapura Kingdom (Sri Lanka): Contemporaneous frontier realm and trading partner.

battles.name: Battle of Venni
battles.parties: Karikala Chola vs. Chera & Pandya Confederacy
battles.summary: Young Karikala decisively defeated the combined armies of the Chera king, Pandya king, and eleven Velir chieftains; the wounded Chera king committed ritual suicide (Vadakkiruthal).

battles.name: Battle of Vatapi
battles.parties: Narasimhavarman I Pallava vs. Pulakeshin II Chalukya
battles.summary: Pallava General Paranjothi stormed and burned the Chalukya cliff fortress of Vatapi; Pulakeshin II fell in defense of his capital, and Narasimhavarman assumed the title Vatapikonda.

battles.name: Battle of Sri Purambiyam
battles.parties: Aparajita Pallava & Aditya I Chola vs. Varagunavarman II Pandya
battles.summary: Decisive three-way collision near Kumbakonam. Ganga king Prithvipati I died heroically; Pandya invasion shattered, sparking the resurrection of the Imperial Chola dynasty.

battles.name: Battle of Takkolam
battles.parties: Krishna III (Rashtrakuta) & Butuga II vs. Rajaditya Chola
battles.summary: Rashtrakuta allied army invaded the northern Chola territory; Ganga feudatory Butuga shot Crown Prince Rajaditya with a poisoned arrow atop his royal war elephant.

battles.name: Battle of Koppam
battles.parties: Rajadhiraja & Rajendra II Chola vs. Someshvara I Chalukya
battles.summary: Emperor Rajadhiraja was mortally wounded on his elephant; his younger brother Rajendra II rallied the retreating Cholas, crowned himself on the active battlefield, and routed the Western Chalukyas.
battles.source: Manimangalam Inscription of Rajendra Chola II

battles.name: Battle of Kudal-Sangamam
battles.parties: Virarajendra Chola vs. Someshvara I (Western Chalukyas)
battles.summary: Fought at the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers. Virarajendra routed Someshvara's sons and generals, erecting a pillar of victory at the confluence.

battles.name: Chola Naval Conquest of Anuradhapura
battles.parties: Rajaraja Chola I vs. King Mahinda V of Sri Lanka
battles.summary: Rajaraja dispatched an armada across the Palk Strait, sacked the ancient capital of Anuradhapura, and established Polonnaruwa as the Chola provincial capital.

battles.name: Chola Expedition to the Ganga
battles.parties: Rajendra Chola I vs. Mahipala I (Pala Empire of Bengal)
battles.summary: Chola expeditionary force marched north through Odisha to the banks of the sacred Ganga, defeating Pala king Mahipala and carrying holy water to consecrate Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
battles.source: Tirumalai Rock Inscription of Rajendra Chola I

events.title: Tamil Sangam Academies of Madurai & Cosmopolitan Poet Tradition
events.desc: Poets assemble Etuttogai and Pattuppattu anthologies celebrating universal human kinship ('Every town is our home town, every human is kin').

shloka.text: யாதும் ஊரே யாவரும் கேளிர் தீதும் நன்றும் பிறர்தர வாரா ॥
shloka.transliteration: Yātum ūrē yāvarum kēḷir tītum naṉṟum piṟartara vārā ||
shloka.translation: Every town is our hometown, and every human being is our kinsman; neither good nor ill comes solely from strangers.

events.title: Roman Aurii Maritime Commerce at Muziris, Korkai & Puhar
events.desc: Yavana vessels cross monsoon winds for black pepper, pearls, and beryl, while Pattinappalai describes bustling Puhar customs warehouses.

shloka.text: கடலோடா கால்வல் நெடுந்தேர் கடலோடும் நாவாயும் ஓடா நிலத்து ॥
shloka.transliteration: Kaṭalōṭā kālval neṭuntēr kaṭalōṭum nāvāyum ōṭā nilattu ||
shloka.translation: Even the stoutest-wheeled war chariot cannot sail across the ocean, nor can the sea-going merchant vessel run upon dry earth—master the proper arena of action.

events.title: Karikala Chola Wins Battle of Venni & Builds the Kallanai (Grand Anicut)
events.desc: Constructs an unyielding stone weir across the Kaveri delta—one of the world's oldest surviving water-diversion dams still in use.

shloka.text: பிணியின்மை செல்வம் விளைவின்பம் ஏமம் அணியென்ப நாட்டிற்கிவ் வைந்து ॥
shloka.transliteration: Piṇiyiṉmai celvam viḷaiviṉpam ēmam aṇiyeṉpa nāṭṭiṟkiv vaintu ||
shloka.translation: Freedom from disease, abundant wealth, fertile harvests, civic happiness, and unfailing security—these five are the true jewels of a great nation.

events.title: Tiruvalluvar Composes the Universal Couplets of the Tirukkuṟaḷ
events.desc: 1,330 Tamil couplets synthesize virtue (Aram), sovereign statecraft (Porul), and human ethics in luminous aphoristic poetry.

shloka.text: படைகுடி கூழமைச்சு நட்பரண் ஆறும் உடையான் அரசருள் ஏறு ॥
shloka.transliteration: Paṭaikuṭi kūḻamaiccu naṭparaṇ āṟum uṭaiyāṉ aracaruḷ ēṟu ||
shloka.translation: An army, loyal subjects, abundant wealth, wise ministers, allies, and strong citadels—the sovereign who commands these six pillars stands as a lion among kings.

events.title: Mahendravarman I Pioneers Rock-Cut Cave Temples & Mattavilasa Sanskrit Drama
events.desc: Excavates Mandagapattu and Mamandur cave shrines declaring his granite art free of brick, timber, or mortar.

shloka.text: प्रज्ञा-दान-दयानुभाव-धृतयः कान्ति-कला-कौशलं सत्यं शौर्यम् अमायता विनय इत्येवंप्रकारा गुणाः ॥
shloka.transliteration: prajñā-dāna-dayānubhāva-dhṛtayaḥ kānti-kalā-kauśalaṁ satyaṁ śauryam amāyatā vinaya ityevaṁprakārā guṇāḥ ||
shloka.translation: Wisdom, munificence, compassion, majesty, fortitude, artistry in sculpture and letters, truth, valor, and humility—all sought shelter in Pallava sovereign Mahendravarman I.
shloka.citation: Mattavilāsa Prahasanam, Nāndī 3 (King Mahendravarman I, Kanchipuram)

events.title: Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) Storms Vatapi & Carves Mamallapuram Monuments
events.desc: Pallava forces defeat Chalukya Pulakeshin II at Vatapi and sculpt the Five Rathas, Shore Temple, and Arjuna's Penance along the Coromandel.

shloka.text: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
shloka.transliteration: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ | sa yatpramāṇaṁ kurute lokastadanuvartate ||
shloka.translation: Whatever lofty standard the sovereign exemplar sets by conduct, the common folk emulate; whatever rule the wise ruler establishes, the realm follows.
shloka.citation: Bhagavad Gītā 3.21 & Cāṇakya Nīti 13.8 ('Yathā Rājā Tathā Prajāḥ')

events.title: Rashtrakuta Monolithic Kailasanatha Temple Excavated at Ellora
events.desc: Krishna I's master sculptors carve a towering multi-storey temple downward out of a single basalt cliff.

shloka.text: वागर्थाविव सम्पृक्तौ वागर्थप्रतिपत्तये । जगतः पितरौ वन्दे पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ ॥
shloka.transliteration: vāgarthāviva sampṛktau vāgarthapratipattaye | jagataḥ pitarau vande pārvatīparameśvarau ||
shloka.translation: Inseparable as word and its meaning, I bow to Parvati and Parameshvara, the eternal parents of the cosmos, for illumination in eloquence and truth.

events.title: Vijayalaya Chola Captures Thanjavur, Founding the Imperial Chola Dynasty
events.desc: Rises along the Kaveri floodplains to revive Chola hegemony over Tondaimandalam and the eastern littoral.

shloka.text: கற்க கசடறக் கற்பவை கற்றபின் நிற்க அதற்குத் தக ॥
shloka.transliteration: Kaṟka kacaṭaṟak kaṟpavai kaṟṟapiṉ niṟka ataṟkut taka ||
shloka.translation: Learn faultlessly whatever is worthy to be learned, and having mastered it, stand steadfastly in conduct worthy of that wisdom.

events.title: Parantaka Chola I Inscribes the Kudavolai Constitutional Charter at Uttaramerur
events.desc: Codifies secret pot-ballot village elections, eligibility age/education norms, term rotation, and mandatory financial audits.

shloka.text: குடவோலை முறைமைப்படி வாரிப்பெருமக்களாய் ஆண்டுதோறும்... ஊரிலுள்ள மகாசபையார் முன்னிலையில் ஓலை பறிப்பித்து ॥
shloka.transliteration: Kuṭavōlai muṟaimaippaṭi vāripperumakkaḷāy āṇṭutōṟum... mahāsapaiyār muṉṉilaiyil ōlai paṟippittu ||
shloka.translation: By secret palm-leaf pot-ballot (Kudavolai), audited village electors shall choose annual administrative committees before the full Mahasabha assembly, barring anyone without spotless fiscal accounts.
shloka.citation: Uttaramerūr Constitutional Inscription of Parāntaka Cōḻa I (921 CE)

events.title: Reign of Rajaraja Chola I & Consecration of the Brihadisvara Temple
events.desc: Completes systematic land revenue surveys, conquers northern Sri Lanka, and raises the 66-meter granite Brihadisvara Vimana in Thanjavur.

shloka.text: திருமகள் போலப் பெருநிலச் செல்வியுந் தனக்கே உரிமை பூண்டமை மனக்கொளக் காந்தளூர்ச் சாலை கலமறுத்தருளி... இராஜராஜேஸ்வரம் எடுத்தருளிய ஸ்ரீராஜராஜ தேவர் ॥
shloka.transliteration: Tirumakaḷ pōlap perunilac celviyun taṉakkē urimai pūṇṭamai maṉakkoḷak Kāntaḷūrc cālai kalam-aṟuttaruḷi... Rājarājēśvaram eṭuttaruḷiya Śrī Rājarāja Dēvar ||
shloka.translation: Emperor Rajaraja Chola I—beloved of Earth and Fortune alike—who shattered the western fleet at Kandalur Salai, surveyed every village revenue boundary, and raised the granite Brihadisvara sanctuary at Thanjavur.
shloka.citation: Brihadīśvara Temple South Wall Meikeerthi (1010 CE)

events.title: Rajendra Chola I Marches to the Ganga & Founds Gangaikondacholapuram
events.desc: Purifies a sacred Liquid Pillar of Victory filled with Ganga water beside a towering Chola-era temple and irrigation lake.

shloka.text: इमं मे गङ्गे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि स्तोमं सचता परुष्ण्या ।
shloka.transliteration: imaṁ me gaṅge yamune sarasvati śutudri stomaṁ sacatā paruṣṇyā |
shloka.translation: Accept my hymn of praise, O sacred rivers Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Sutudri (Sutlej), along with Parushni (Ravi), Asikni, and Vitasta (Jhelum).

events.title: Trans-Oceanic Chola Naval Expedition to Srivijaya (Malaya & Sumatra)
events.desc: Blue-water Chola armada sails across the Bay of Bengal, subjugating Kedah and Palembang to protect maritime trade guilds to Song China.

shloka.text: नानाश्रान्ताय श्रीरस्तीति रोहित शुश्रुम । पापो नृषद्वरो जन इन्द्र इच्चरतः सखा । चरैवेति चरैवेति ॥
shloka.transliteration: nānāśrāntāya śrīrastīti rohita śuśruma | pāpo nṛṣadvaro jana indra iccarataḥ sakhā | caraiveti caraiveti ||
shloka.translation: Fortune never favors one who refuses to strive forward; Indra himself befriends the tireless explorer—therefore march onward, march onward!

shloka_epigraph.text:
யாதும் ஊரே யாவரும் கேளிர்
தீதும் நன்றும் பிறர்தர வாரா
நோதலும் தணிதலும் அவற்றோ ரன்ன
சாதலும் புதுவது அன்றே... பெரியோரை வியத்தலும் இலமே
சிறியோரை இகழ்தல் அதனினும் இலமே ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation:
"Every town is our home; everyone is our kin.
Good and evil come not from others.
Pain and relief follow their own course.
Death is not a novel thing... We do not marvel at the great,
Much less do we disdain the small."
shloka_epigraph.citation: Purananuru, poem 192, composed by Kaniyan Pungundranar
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: U.V. Swaminatha Iyer Critical Sangam Edition (1894)

empires.historical_map_title: The Imperial Cholas — Rājarāja I & Rājendra I (c. 985–1150 CE)

detailed_history.overview: The classical civilizations of peninsular South India flourished through a succession of maritime empires: the Sangam Era Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas (c. 300 BCE – 300 CE), the rock-carving Pallavas of Kanchipuram (c. 300–900 CE), the imperial Western Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas of the Deccan (c. 543–982 CE), and the zenith of the Imperial Cholas under Rajaraja I and Rajendra I (c. 985–1150 CE). Commanding Indian Ocean seafaring from the Coromandel coast to Srivijaya (Indonesia/Malaysia), these dynasties created monumental granite temples (Brihadisvara), exquisite lost-wax Nataraja bronzes, and democratic village assemblies.

chronicle.era: c. 300 BCE – 300 CE: The Sangam Age & Oceanic Commerce
chronicle.narrative: The Muventhar (Three Crowned Kings—Chera, Chola, Pandya) patronized the Tamil Sangam academies at Madurai. As recorded in the Purananuru and the Greco-Roman Periplus, ports like Muziris, Korkai, and Puhar (Kaveripattinam) exported black pepper, beryl, and pearls directly to imperial Rome and Alexandria in exchange for gold dinarii.

chronicle.era: c. 575 – 850 CE: Pallavas & Early Chalukyas
chronicle.narrative: Simhavishnu and Mahendravarman I established Pallava hegemony from Kanchipuram, carving monolithic rock temples (rathas and Shore Temple) at Mamallapuram. Their centuries-long rivalry with the Chalukyas of Badami (Pulakeshin II, Vikramaditya II) and later the Rashtrakutas of Manyakheta (who carved the monolithic Kailash Temple at Ellora) catalyzed Deccan Dravidian architecture.

chronicle.era: c. 985 – 1150 CE: The Imperial Cholas & Trans-Oceanic Thassalocracy
chronicle.narrative: Rajaraja Chola I (r. 985–1014 CE) unified southern India, conquered Sri Lanka (Anuradhapura), and erected the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur. His son Rajendra Chola I (r. 1014–1044 CE) marched to the banks of the sacred Ganga (earning the title Gangaikondachola) and launched a trans-oceanic naval expedition across the Bay of Bengal, sacking the Srivijaya maritime empire in Sumatra and Malaya to safeguard the spice trade routes to Song Dynasty China.

primary_sources.source_title: Brihadīśvara Temple South Wall Inscription of Rājarāja Cōḻa I (Thanjavur)
primary_sources.original_text: திருமகள் போலப் பெருநிலச் செல்வியுந் தனக்கே யுரிமை பூண்டமை மனக்கொளக் காந்தளூர்ச் சாலை கலமறுத்தருளி... வேங்கை நாடும் கங்கபாடியும் தடிகைபாடியும் நுளம்பபாடியும் குடமலை நாடும் கொல்லமும் கலிங்கமும்... ஈழ மண்டலமும் இரட்டபாடி ஏழரை இலக்கமும் திண்டிறல் வென்றித் தண்டாற் கொண்ட தன்னெழில் வளரூழி...
primary_sources.transliteration: Tirumakaḷ pōlap perunilac celviyun tanakkē yurimai pūṇṭamai maṉakkoḷak Kāntaḷūrc cālai kalam-aṟuttaruḷi... Vēṅkai nāṭum Kaṅkapāṭiyum Taṭikaipāṭiyum Nuḷampapāṭiyum Kuṭamalai nāṭum Kollamum Kaliṅgamum... Īḻa maṇṭalamum Iraṭṭapāṭi ēḻarai ilakkamum tiṇṭiṟal veṉṟit taṇṭāṟ koṇṭa tan-neḻil vaḷar-ūḻi...
primary_sources.translation: While the Goddess of Fortune, even like the Goddess of the Great Earth, had become his exclusive bride... he destroyed the fleet of Kandalur Salai; by his powerful, victorious army he conquered Vengai Nadu, Gangapadi, Tadigai-padi, Nulambapadi, Kudamalai Nadu, Kollam, Kalingam... Ilam (Sri Lanka) surrounded by the deep sea, and the seven and a half lakh country of Rattapadi (Chalukyas)... he erected this stone temple for the Lord of the Universe (Rajarajesvaram).
primary_sources.academic_citation: South Indian Inscriptions, Vol. II, Part I, No. 1, pp. 1–14; K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Colas, University of Madras, 1955, pp. 168–190.
primary_sources.significance: The celebrated opening Meikeerthi (royal eulogy) of Rajaraja Chola recording his military campaigns and the dedication of the Brihadisvara Granite Temple.

primary_sources.source_title: Uttaramerūr Inscription of Parāntaka Cōḻa I (Vaikuntha Perumal Temple)
primary_sources.original_text: குடவோலை முறைமைப்படி வாரிப்பெருமக்களாய் ஆண்டுதோறும்... குடவோலை பறிக்கும்போது ஊரிலுள்ள மகாசபையார் முன்னிலையில் பையன் ஒருவனைக் கொண்டு ஓலை பறிப்பித்து...
primary_sources.transliteration: Kuṭavōlai muṟaimaippaṭi vāripperumakkaḷāy āṇṭutōṟum... kuṭavōlai paṟikkumpōtu ūrilluḷḷa mahāsapaiyār muṉṉilaiyil paiyaṉ oruvaṉaik koṇṭu ōlai paṟippittu...
primary_sources.translation: According to the system of secret pot-ballot (Kudavolai), every year the ward committees shall be chosen: when the pot-tickets are drawn, in the presence of the full village assembly (Mahasabha), a young boy who knows nothing of the names shall draw out the palm-leaf ballots from the pot... Any candidate who has not submitted accounts of expenditure during his term shall be disqualified along with his relatives.
primary_sources.academic_citation: Archaeological Survey of India Annual Report 1904–1905, pp. 131–145; R. Nagaswamy, Studies in Ancient Tamil Law & Society, Department of Archaeology, Government of Tamil Nadu, 1978.
primary_sources.significance: World-famous constitutional inscription demonstrating democratic local self-governance, secret ballot elections, ethical term limits, and audit procedures in 10th-century Tamil Nadu.

locations.name: Thanjavur
locations.role: Imperial Chola capital; site of Rajaraja's Brihadisvara Temple
locations.desc: Granary of Tamilakam and administrative seat of the Middle Chola Empire.

locations.name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram
locations.role: New imperial capital built by Rajendra Chola I after victorious northern march
locations.desc: Founded 1025 CE with the vast Cholaganga irrigation reservoir ('Liquid Pillar of Victory').

locations.name: Madurai
locations.role: Ancient Pandya capital on the Vaigai river
locations.desc: Sacred center of the three legendary Tamil Sangam literary assemblies and the Meenakshi temple.

locations.name: Kanchipuram
locations.role: Grand Pallava capital and educational center (Ghatika)
locations.desc: City of a thousand temples; capital of Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I.

locations.name: Mamallapuram
locations.role: Pallava royal seaport with monolithic rock-cut rathas and Shore Temple
locations.desc: Emporium of Pallava maritime trade with Southeast Asia and China.

locations.name: Muziris (Kodungallur)
locations.role: Foremost Chera international port on the Malabar Coast
locations.desc: Where Roman ships brought gold and wine to exchange for Malabar black pepper and beryl.

locations.name: Korkai
locations.role: Ancient Pandya pearl-fishery port at the mouth of the Thamirabarani
locations.desc: Celebrated in Sangam poems and Greco-Roman texts for the world's finest sea pearls.

locations.name: Uraiyur (Tiruchirappalli)
locations.role: Early Sangam Chola capital noted for fine handloom textiles
locations.desc: Ancient fortress capital of Karikala Chola on the southern bank of the Kaveri.

locations.name: Puhar / Kaveripattinam
locations.role: Fabled Sangam Chola seaport emporium celebrated in Silappadikaram
locations.desc: Cosmopolitan harbor with foreign merchant colonies, lighthouses, and dockyards.

locations.name: Vatapi (Badami)
locations.role: Rock-cut cliff capital of the Early Western Chalukyas
locations.desc: Seat of Pulakeshin II surrounded by red sandstone cliff temples and Lake Agastya.

locations.name: Manyakheta (Malkhed)
locations.role: Imperial capital of the Rashtrakuta Empire
locations.desc: Founded by Amoghavarsha I; celebrated by Arab merchant Sulaiman as one of the four great empires of the world.

locations.name: Vengi
locations.role: Capital of the Eastern Chalukyas; contested Chola-Chalukya buffer
locations.desc: Strategic territory linking the Tamil heartland to Odisha and Bengal.

locations.name: Anuradhapura (Sri Lanka)
locations.role: Ancient Sinhala capital conquered by Rajaraja Chola I
locations.desc: Incorporated into the Chola Empire as the province of Mummudi-Chola-Mandalam in 993 CE.
